      "verbatim_text": "8.4.24 Fr_GetWakeupRxStatus\n[SWS_Fr_00587] Definition of API function Fr_GetWakeupRxStatus ⌈\nService Name\nFr_GetWakeupRxStatus\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType Fr_GetWakeupRxStatus (\nuint8 Fr_CtrlIdx,\nuint8* Fr_WakeupRxStatusPtr\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x2b\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nNon Reentrant for the same device\nParameters (in)\nFr_CtrlIdx\nIndex of FlexRay CC within the context of the FlexRay Driver.\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nFr_WakeupRxStatusPtr\nAddress where bitcoded wakeup reception status shall be stored.\nBit 0: Wakeup received on channel A indicator Bit 1: Wakeup\nreceived on channel B indicator Bit 2-7: Unused\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: API call finished successfully.\nE_NOT_OK: API call aborted due to errors.\nDescription\nGets the wakeup received information from the FlexRay controller.\nAvailable via\nFr.h\n⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00588] ⌈The function Fr_GetWakeupRxStatus() shall perform the follow-\ning tasks on FlexRay CC Fr_CtrIdx:\n1. Read the wakeup pattern received indicators for channel A and channel B\nand write it to the output parameter Fr_WakeupRxStatusPtr. The value of\n*Fr_WakeupRxStatusPtr is bitcoded with the following meaning (Bit 0 = LSB,\nBit 7 = MSB):\nBit 0 Wakeup pattern received on channel A (1), otherwise (0)\nBit 1 Wakeup pattern received on channel B (1), otherwise (0)\nBit 2 Not used (always 0)\nBit 3 Not used (always 0)\nBit 4 Not used (always 0)\nBit 5 Not used (always 0)\nBit 6 Not used (always 0)\nBit 7 Not used (always 0)\n2. Reset the wakeup received indication status information within the FlexRay con-\ntroller.\n3. Return E_OK.\n⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00589]\n⌈If\nthe\nfunction\nFr_GetWakeupRxStatus()\nis\nable\nto\nand\ndetects\na\nhardware\nerror\nwhile\nperforming\nthe\nrequested\nfunctional-\nity,\nthen\nit\nshall\ncall\nDem_SetEventStatus()\n(FR_E_CTRL_TESTRESULT,\nDEM_EVENT_STATUS_FAILED) and return E_NOT_OK.⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00590] ⌈If development error detection for the Fr module is enabled, and if\nthe function Fr_GetWakeupRxStatus() is called before the successful initialization\nof Fr, then the function Fr_GetWakeupRxStatus() shall raise the development error\nFR_E_INIT_FAILED.⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00591] ⌈If development error detection for the Fr module is enabled, then\nthe function Fr_GetWakeupRxStatus() shall check the validity of the parameter\nFr_CtrlIdx. If Fr_CtrlIdx is invalid, then the function Fr_GetWakeupRxSta-\ntus() shall raise the development error FR_E_INV_CTRL_IDX.⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00592]\n⌈If\ndevelopment\nerror\ndetection\nfor\nthe\nFr\nmodule\nis\nen-\nabled,\nthen\nthe\nfunction\nFr_GetWakeupRxStatus()\nshall\ncheck\nwhether\nthe\nparameter\nFr_WakeupRxStatusPtr\nis\na\nNULL\npointer\n(NULL_PTR).\nIf\nFr_WakeupRxStatusPtr is a NULL pointer, then the function Fr_GetWake-\nupRxStatus() shall raise the development error FR_E_PARAM_POINTER.⌋"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "8.4.2 Fr_ControllerInit\n[SWS_Fr_00017] Definition of API function Fr_ControllerInit\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Fr_05116, SRS_Fr_05011\n⌈\nService Name\nFr_ControllerInit\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType Fr_ControllerInit (\nuint8 Fr_CtrlIdx\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x00\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nNon Reentrant for the same device\nParameters (in)\nFr_CtrlIdx\nIndex of FlexRay CC within the context of the FlexRay Driver.\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: API call finished successfully.\nE_NOT_OK: API call aborted due to errors.\nDescription\nInitialzes a FlexRay CC.\nAvailable via\nFr.h\n⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00148]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Fr_05059, SRS_Fr_05012\n⌈The function Fr_ControllerInit() shall perform the following tasks on FlexRay\nCC Fr_CtrIdx:\n1. Switch CC into ’POC:config’ (from any other POCState).\n2. Configure all FlexRay cluster and node configuration parameters (e.g., cycle\nlength, macrotick duration).\n3. Configure all transmit/receive resources (e.g., buffer initialization) according to\nthe frame triggering configuration parameters contained in the FrIf.\n4. Switch CC into ’POC:ready’\n5. Return E_OK.\n⌋\nCC post condition for the function Fr_ControllerInit(): CC Fr_CtrlIdx shall be\nleft in POCState ’POC:ready’.\n[SWS_Fr_00149] ⌈The function Fr_ControllerInit() shall ensure that no trans-\nmission requests are pending.⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00150] ⌈The function Fr_ControllerInit() shall ensure that no recep-\ntion indications are pending.⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00151] ⌈The function Fr_ControllerInit() shall ensure that no inter-\nrupts are pending.⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00152]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Fr_05169\n⌈The function Fr_ControllerInit() shall ensure that all timers are disabled.⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00153] ⌈The function Fr_ControllerInit() shall ensure that all inter-\nrupts are disabled.⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00515] ⌈The function Fr_ControllerInit() shall disable all LPdus which\nare dynamically reconfigurable (see Fr_ReconfigLPdu(), Fr_DisableLPdu()).⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00147] ⌈If the function Fr_ControllerInit() detects errors while test-\ning the CC (CC test), then it shall repeat the test procedure a configurable number (\nFrCtrlTestCount) of times. If all tests fail, then it calls Dem_SetEventStatus() (\nFR_E_CTRL_TESTRESULT, DEM_EVENT_STATUS_FAILED) and returns E_NOT_OK.⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00647] ⌈The CC test as described in [SWS_Fr_00147] shall verify (read\nback and compare to reference values held in the configuration) that the node and\ncluster FlexRay parameters were written properly into the FlexRay CC.⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00598]\n⌈If\nthe\nfunction\nFr_ControllerInit()\npasses\nthe\nCC\ntest\nwithin\na\nnumber\nof\nconfigurable\n(FrCtrlTestCount)\ntimes,\nthen\nit\ncalls\nDem_SetEventStatus()\n(FR_E_CTRL_TESTRESULT,\nDEM_EVENT_STATUS_PASSED).⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00143] ⌈If development error detection for the Fr module is enabled, and\nif the function Fr_ControllerInit() is called before the successful initialization\nof Fr, then the function Fr_ControllerInit() shall raise the development error\nFR_E_INIT_FAILED.⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00144] ⌈If development error detection for the Fr module is enabled,\nthen the function Fr_ControllerInit() shall check the validity of the parameter\nFr_CtrlIdx. If Fr_CtrlIdx is invalid, then the function Fr_ControllerInit()\nshall raise the development error FR_E_INV_CTRL_IDX.⌋"
    },

If Fr_CtrlIdx is invalid, then the function Fr_GetAbsolute-\nTimerIRQStatus() shall raise the development error FR_E_INV_CTRL_IDX.⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00329] ⌈If development error detection for the Fr module is enabled,\nthen the function Fr_GetAbsoluteTimerIRQStatus() shall check the validity\nof the parameter Fr_AbsTimerIdx.\nIf Fr_AbsTimerIdx is invalid, then the\nfunction Fr_GetAbsoluteTimerIRQStatus() shall raise the development error\nFR_E_INV_TIMER_IDX.⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00330] ⌈If development error detection for the Fr module is enabled, then\nthe function Fr_GetAbsoluteTimerIRQStatus() shall check whether the param-\neter Fr_IRQStatusPtr is a NULL pointer (NULL_PTR).       "verbatim_text": "8.4.32 Fr_ReadCCConfig\n[SWS_Fr_00651] Definition of API function Fr_ReadCCConfig ⌈\nService Name\nFr_ReadCCConfig\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType Fr_ReadCCConfig (\nuint8 Fr_CtrlIdx,\nuint8 Fr_ConfigParamIdx,\nuint32* Fr_ConfigParamValuePtr\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x2e\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nNon Reentrant for the same device\nFr_CtrlIdx\nIndex of FlexRay CC within the context of the FlexRay Driver.\nParameters (in)\nFr_ConfigParamIdx\nIndex that identifies the configuration parameter to read. See\nmacros FR_CIDX_<config_parameter_name>.\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nFr_ConfigParamValuePtr\nAddress the output value is stored to.\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: API call finished successfully.\nE_NOT_OK: API call aborted due to errors.\nDescription\nReads a FlexRay protocol configuration parameter for a particular FlexRay controller out of the\nmodule’s configuration.\nAvailable via\nFr.h\n⌋\nThe function Fr_ReadCCConfig() shall perform the following tasks:\n1. Read\nthe\nvalue\nof\nthe\nconfiguration\nparameter\nrequested\nby\nFr_ConfigParamIdx from the configuration and write it to output param-\neter *Fr_ConfigParamValuePtr.\n2. Return E_OK.\n[SWS_Fr_00652]\n⌈If\nthe\nfunction\nFr_ReadCCConfig()\nis\nable\nto\nand\ndetects\na\nhardware\nerror\nwhile\nperforming\nthe\nrequested\nfunctionality,\nthen\nit\nshall\ncall\nDem_SetEventStatus()\n(FR_E_CTRL_TESTRESULT,\nDEM_EVENT_STATUS_FAILED) and return E_NOT_OK.⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00653] ⌈If development error detection for the Fr module is enabled,\nand if the function Fr_ReadCCConfig() is called before the successful initializa-\ntion of Fr, then the function Fr_ReadCCConfig() shall raise the development error\nFR_E_INIT_FAILED.⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00654] ⌈If development error detection for the Fr module is enabled, then the\nfunction Fr_ReadCCConfig() shall check the validity of the parameter Fr_CtrlIdx.\nIf Fr_CtrlIdx is invalid, then the function Fr_ReadCCConfig() shall raise the devel-\nopment error FR_E_INV_CTRL_IDX.⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00655] ⌈If development error detection for the Fr module is enabled,\nthen the function Fr_ReadCCConfig() shall check the validity of the parameter\nFr_ConfigParamIdx. If Fr_ConfigParamIdx is invalid, then the function Fr_-\nReadCCConfig() shall raise the development error FR_E_INV_CONFIG_IDX.⌋\n13\n[SWS_Fr_00656]\n⌈If\ndevelopment\nerror\ndetection\nfor\nthe\nFr\nmodule\nis\nen-\nabled,\nthen\nthe\nfunction\nFr_ReadCCConfig()\nshall\ncheck\nwhether\nthe\npa-\nrameter\nFr_ConfigParamValuePtr\nis\na\nNULL\npointer\n(NULL_PTR).\nIf\nFr_ConfigParamValuePtr is a NULL pointer, then the function Fr_ReadCC-\nConfig() shall raise the development error FR_E_PARAM_POINTER.⌋\nConfiguration parameters values are specified as integer, float, enumeration or\nboolean. In order to map those values to the output parameter of type uint32, the\nfollowing generic rules for conversion shall be applied for integer and float:\n• [SWS_Fr_00658] ⌈integers are mapped 1 to 1.⌋\n• [SWS_Fr_00659] ⌈floats (units of seconds) are converted to units of nanosec-\nonds (with nanosecond granularity) and converted to uint32.⌋\n• [SWS_Fr_00661] ⌈booleans shall output 1 for true and 0 for false.⌋\nFor configuration parameters specified as enumeration type, the following mappings\nshall be applied:\n[SWS_Fr_00662]\n⌈If\nparameter\nFr_ConfigParamIdx\nis\nset\nto\nFR_CIDX_PCHANNELS\n(FrPChannels)\nthen\nthe\nvalue\nstored\nat\nFr_ConfigParamValuePtr shall be interpreted as the following literals\n13Valid values are listed in Chapter 8.2.1 “Configuration parameter index macros” and and in require-\nments [SWS_Fr_00662], [SWS_Fr_00663], [SWS_Fr_00664], [SWS_Fr_00665], [SWS_Fr_00666].\n0 FR_CHANNEL_A"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "8.4.3 Fr_StartCommunication\n[SWS_Fr_00010] Definition of API function Fr_StartCommunication\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Fr_05109\n⌈\nService Name\nFr_StartCommunication\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType Fr_StartCommunication (\nuint8 Fr_CtrlIdx\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x03\nSync/Async\nAsynchronous\nReentrancy\nNon Reentrant for the same device\nParameters (in)\nFr_CtrlIdx\nIndex of FlexRay CC within the context of the FlexRay Driver.\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: API call finished successfully.\nE_NOT_OK: API call aborted due to errors.\nDescription\nStarts communication.\nAvailable via\nFr.h\n⌋\nNote: The Fr module’s environment shall only call the function Fr_StartCommuni-\ncation() when CC Fr_CtrlIdx is in POCState ’POC:ready’.\n[SWS_Fr_00177] ⌈The function Fr_StartCommunication() shall perform the fol-\nlowing tasks on FlexRay CC Fr_CtrIdx:\n1. Invoke the CC CHI command ’RUN’, which initiates the startup procedure within\nthe FlexRay CC.\n2. Return E_OK.\n⌋\nThe function call of Fr_StartCommunication() changes the CC POCState to\nPOC:startup which is a transitional state. In the case when communication startup\nsucceeds, the CC wil change the POCState to ’POC:normal active’ or ’POC:normal\npassive’. It is not guaranteed that the FlexRay CC will reside in the ’POC:normal active’\nor ’POC:normal passive’ state after a call of the function Fr_StartCommunication().\n[SWS_Fr_00176]\n⌈If\nthe\nfunction\nFr_StartCommunication()\nis\nable\nto\nand\ndetects\na\nhardware\nerror\nwhile\nperforming\nthe\nrequested\nfunctional-\nity,\nthen\nit\nshall\ncall\nDem_SetEventStatus()\n(FR_E_CTRL_TESTRESULT,\nDEM_EVENT_STATUS_FAILED) and return E_NOT_OK.⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00173] ⌈If development error detection for the Fr module is enabled, and\nif the function Fr_StartCommunication() is called before successful initialization\nof the Fr, then the function Fr_StartCommunication() shall raise the development\nerror FR_E_INIT_FAILED.⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00174] ⌈If development error detection for the Fr module is enabled, and\nthe function Fr_StartCommunication() shall check the validity of the parameter\nFr_CtrlIdx. If Fr_CtrlIdx is invalid, then the function Fr_StartCommunica-\ntion() shall raise the development error FR_E_INV_CTRL_IDX.⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00175] ⌈The function Fr_StartCommunication() shall check whether\nthe CC Fr_CtrlIdx’s POCState is in POC:ready.\nIf the POCState is not\nPOC:ready, then the function Fr_StartCommunication() shall raise the runtime er-\nror FR_E_INV_POCSTATE.⌋"
    },

Invoke the CC CHI command ’ALLOW_COLDSTART’.\n2. If Fr_CtrlIdx is invalid, then the function Fr_AllowColdstart()\nshall raise the development error FR_E_INV_CTRL_IDX.⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00180]\n⌈The\nfunction\nFr_AllowColdstart()\nshall\ncheck\nthe\nCC\nFr_CtrlIdx’s POCState.\nIf the POCState is POC:default config, POC:config, or\nPOC:halt, then the function Fr_AllowColdstart() shall raise the runtime error\nFR_E_INV_POCSTATE.⌋"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "8.4.7 Fr_AbortCommunication\n[SWS_Fr_00011] Definition of API function Fr_AbortCommunication\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Fr_05114\n⌈\nService Name\nFr_AbortCommunication\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType Fr_AbortCommunication (\nuint8 Fr_CtrlIdx\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x05\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nNon Reentrant for the same device\nParameters (in)\nFr_CtrlIdx\nIndex of FlexRay CC within the context of the FlexRay Driver.\n▽\n2Invoke the command ’HALT’ for FlexRay Controllers compliant to [2].\n△\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: API call finished successfully.\nE_NOT_OK: API call aborted due to errors.\nDescription\nInvokes the CC CHI command ’FREEZE’.\nAvailable via\nFr.h\n⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00191] ⌈The function Fr_AbortCommunication() shall perform the fol-\nlowing tasks on FlexRay CC Fr_CtrIdx:\n• Invoke the CC CHI command ’FREEZE’, which immediately aborts communica-\ntion (if active) and changes to the POC:halt state from any previous POCState.\n• Return E_OK.\n⌋\nNote: The function Fr_AbortCommunication() leaves the CC Fr_CtrlIdx in POC-\nState POC:halt (vPOC!Freeze is set).\n[SWS_Fr_00190]\n⌈If\nthe\nfunction\nFr_AbortCommunication()\nis\nable\nto\nand\ndetects\na\nhardware\nerror\nwhile\nperforming\nthe\nrequested\nfunctional-\nity,\nthen\nit\nshall\ncall\nDem_SetEventStatus()\n(FR_E_CTRL_TESTRESULT,\nDEM_EVENT_STATUS_FAILED) and return E_NOT_OK.⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00188] ⌈If development error detection for the Fr module is enabled, and if\nthe function Fr_AbortCommunication() is called before the successful initialization\nof Fr, then the function Fr_AbortCommunication() shall raise the development error\nFR_E_INIT_FAILED.⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00189] ⌈If development error detection for the Fr module is enabled, then\nthe function Fr_AbortCommunication() shall check the validity of the parameter\nFr_CtrlIdx. If Fr_CtrlIdx is invalid, then the function Fr_AbortCommunica-\ntion() shall raise the development error FR_E_INV_CTRL_IDX.⌋"

      "verbatim_text": "8.4.8 Fr_SendWUP\n[SWS_Fr_00009] Definition of API function Fr_SendWUP\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Fr_05117\n⌈\nService Name\nFr_SendWUP\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType Fr_SendWUP (\nuint8 Fr_CtrlIdx\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x06\nSync/Async\nAsynchronous\nReentrancy\nNon Reentrant for the same device\nParameters (in)\nFr_CtrlIdx\nIndex of FlexRay CC within the context of the FlexRay Driver.\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: API call finished successfully.\nE_NOT_OK: API call aborted due to errors.\nDescription\nInvokes the CC CHI command ’WAKEUP’.\nAvailable via\nFr.h\n⌋\nNote:\nThe Fr module’s environment shall only call Fr_SendWUP() when CC\nFr_CtrlIdx is in POCState ’POC:ready’.\n[SWS_Fr_00196] ⌈The function Fr_SendWUP() shall perform the following tasks on\nFlexRay CC Fr_CtrIdx:\n1. Invoke the CC CHI command ’WAKEUP’, which initiates the wakeup transmission\nprocedure on the configured FlexRay channel.\n2. Return E_OK.\n⌋\nNote:\nThe function Fr_SendWUP() changes the CC Fr_CtrlIdx POCState to\nPOC:wakeup, which is a transitional state. After wakeup procedure completion, the\nCC will reach POC:ready again.\nNote: Sending a wakeup pattern does not necessarily cause all cluster nodes to be\nawoken afterwards. The function Fr_SendWUP() just invokes the wakeup symbol trans-\nmission procedure on a certain FlexRay CC.\n[SWS_Fr_00195]\n⌈If\nthe\nfunction\nFr_SendWUP()\nis\nable\nto\nand\nde-\ntects\na\nhardware\nerror\nwhile\nperforming\nthe\nrequested\nfunctionality,\nthen\nit\nshall\ncall\nDem_SetEventStatus()\n(FR_E_CTRL_TESTRESULT,\nDEM_EVENT_STATUS_FAILED) and return E_NOT_OK.⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00192] ⌈If development error detection for the Fr module is enabled, and if\nthe function Fr_SendWUP() is called before the successful initialization of Fr, then the\nfunction Fr_SendWUP() shall raise the development error FR_E_INIT_FAILED.⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00193] ⌈If development error detection for the Fr module is enabled, then\nthe function Fr_SendWUP() shall check the validity of the parameter Fr_CtrlIdx. If\nFr_CtrlIdx is invalid, then the function Fr_SendWUP() shall raise the development\nerror FR_E_INV_CTRL_IDX.⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00194]\n⌈The\nfunction\nFr_SendWUP()\nshall\ncheck\nwhether\nthe\nCC\nFr_CtrlIdx’s POCState is POC:ready. If the POCState is not POC:ready, then the\nfunction Fr_SendWUP() shall raise the runtime error FR_E_INV_POCSTATE.⌋"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "8.4.9 Fr_SetWakeupChannel\n[SWS_Fr_00091] Definition of API function Fr_SetWakeupChannel\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Fr_05117\n⌈\nService Name\nFr_SetWakeupChannel\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType Fr_SetWakeupChannel (\nuint8 Fr_CtrlIdx,\nFr_ChannelType Fr_ChnlIdx\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x07\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nNon Reentrant for the same device\nFr_CtrlIdx\nIndex of FlexRay CC within the context of the FlexRay Driver.\nParameters (in)\nFr_ChnlIdx\nIndex of FlexRay channel within the context of the FlexRay CC\nFr_CtrlIdx. Valid values are FR_CHANNEL_A and FR_\nCHANNEL_B.\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: API call finished successfully.\nE_NOT_OK: API call aborted due to errors.\nDescription\nSets a wakeup channel.\nAvailable via\nFr.h\n⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00202] ⌈The function Fr_SetWakeupChannel() shall perform the following\ntasks on FlexRay CC Fr_CtrIdx:\n1. Change the CC’s POCState to POC:config by invoking the CHI command ’CON-\nFIG’.\n2. Configure the wakeup channel according to parameter Fr_ChnlIdx.\n3. Change the CC’s POCState to POC:ready again by invoking the CHI command\n’CONFIG_COMPLETE’.\n4. Return E_OK.\n⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00201]\n⌈If\nthe\nfunction\nFr_SetWakeupChannel()\nis\nable\nto\nand\ndetects\na\nhardware\nerror\nwhile\nperforming\nthe\nrequested\nfunctional-\nity,\nthen\nit\nshall\ncall\nDem_SetEventStatus()\n(FR_E_CTRL_TESTRESULT,\nDEM_EVENT_STATUS_FAILED) and return E_NOT_OK.⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00197] ⌈If development error detection for the Fr module is enabled, and\nif the function Fr_SetWakeupChannel() is called before the successful initialization\nof Fr, then the function Fr_SetWakeupChannel() shall raise the development error\nFR_E_INIT_FAILED.⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00198] ⌈If development error detection for the Fr module is enabled, then\nthe function Fr_SetWakeupChannel() shall check the validity of the parameter\nFr_CtrlIdx. If Fr_CtrlIdx is invalid, then the function Fr_SetWakeupChannel()\nshall raise the development error FR_E_INV_CTRL_IDX.⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00199] ⌈If development error detection for the Fr module is enabled, then\nthe function Fr_SetWakeupChannel() shall check the validity of the parameter\nFr_ChnlIdx. If Fr_ChnlIdx is invalid, then the function Fr_SetWakeupChannel()\nshall raise the development error FR_E_INV_CHNL_IDX.⌋\n[SWS_Fr_00200] ⌈The function Fr_SetWakeupChannel() shall check whether\nthe\nCC\nFr_CtrlIdx’s\nPOCState\nis\nPOC:ready.\nIf\nthe\nPOCState\nis\nnot\n’POC:ready’, then the function Fr_SetWakeupChannel() shall raise the runtime error\nFR_E_INV_POCSTATE.⌋"

      "verbatim_text": "8.4 Function definitions\nDuring specification of the API functions the following guidelines were applied:\n• The API functions of the Fr module shall have the return type Std_ReturnType\nor void (no return code).\n• If an API function of the Fr module has the return type Std_ReturnType, and if\nthe function performs its service successfully, then it shall return E_OK otherwise\nE_NOT_OK.\n• If the Fr module’s environment is passing input parameters by a reference, then\nthe Fr SWS shall use the const qualifier (const type *) to guarantee that it\ndoesn’t change the input parameter.\n• For output parameters, a memory address to store the parameter is passed as\nan argument.\n• If API functions of the Fr module successfully finish (return E_OK), then all output\nparameters shall be written with with valid values.\n• If API functions of the Fr module erroneously finish (return E_NOT_OK), then no\noutput parameter shall be written. Output parameters shall keep their original\nvalues in this case."
    },

      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "8.8.1 Mandatory Interfaces\nThis chapter defines all API services which are required from other BSW modules to\nfulfill the core functionality of the FlexRay Interface.\n[SWS_FrIf_05043] Definition of mandatory interfaces in module FrIf ⌈\nAPI Function\nHeader File\nDescription\nDet_ReportRuntimeError\nDet.h\nService to report runtime errors. If a callout has\nbeen configured then this callout shall be called.\nFr_AbortCommunication\nFr.h\nInvokes the CC CHI command ’FREEZE’.\nFr_AckAbsoluteTimerIRQ\nFr.h\nResets the interrupt condition of an absolute timer.\nFr_AllowColdstart\nFr.h\nInvokes the CC CHI command ’ALLOW_\nCOLDSTART’.\nFr_CancelAbsoluteTimer\nFr.h\nStops an absolute timer.\nFr_CheckTxLPduStatus\nFr.h\nChecks the transmit status of the LSdu.\nFr_ControllerInit\nFr.h\nInitialzes a FlexRay CC.\nFr_DisableAbsoluteTimerIRQ\nFr.h\nDisables the interrupt line of an absolute timer.\nFr_EnableAbsoluteTimerIRQ\nFr.h\nEnables the interrupt line of an absolute timer.\nFr_GetAbsoluteTimerIRQStatus\nFr.h\nGets IRQ status of an absolute timer.\nFr_GetGlobalTime\nFr.h\nGets the current global FlexRay time.\nImportant Note: Fr_GetGlobalTime may be called\nwithin an exclusive area.\nFr_GetPOCStatus\nFr.h\nGets the POC status.\nFr_HaltCommunication\nFr.h\nInvokes the CC CHI command ’DEFERRED_HALT’.\nFr_ReceiveRxLPdu\nFr.h\nReceives data from the FlexRay network.\nFr_SendWUP\nFr.h\nInvokes the CC CHI command ’WAKEUP’.\nFr_SetAbsoluteTimer\nFr.h\nSets the absolute FlexRay timer.\nFr_SetWakeupChannel\nFr.h\nSets a wakeup channel.\nFr_StartCommunication\nFr.h\nStarts communication.\nFr_TransmitTxLPdu\nFr.h\nTransmits data on the FlexRay network.\nFrTrcv_CheckWakeupByTransceiver\nFrTrcv.h\n–\nFrTrcv_ClearTransceiverWakeup\nFrTrcv.h\nThis function clears a pending wake up event.\nFrTrcv_GetTransceiverMode\nFrTrcv.h\nThis function returns the actual state of the\ntransceiver.\nFrTrcv_GetTransceiverWUReason\nFrTrcv.h\nThis function returns the wakeup reason.\nFrTrcv_SetTransceiverMode\nFrTrcv.h\nThis service sets the transceiver mode.\n⌋()"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_FR_SECTION_8_8_2_Optional_Interfaces",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_FlexRayInterface",
      "source_page": 97,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "8.8.2 Optional Interfaces\nThis chapter defines all API services which are required from other BSW modules to\nfulfill an optional functionality of the FlexRay Interface\n[SWS_FrIf_05044] Definition of optional interfaces requested by module FrIf ⌈\nAPI Function\nHeader File\nDescription\nDem_SetEventStatus\nDem.h\nCalled by SW-Cs or BSW modules to report monitor\nstatus information to the Dem. BSW modules calling\nDem_SetEventStatus can safely ignore the return\nvalue. This API will be available only if ({Dem/Dem\nConfigSet/DemEventParameter/DemEvent\nReportingType} == STANDARD_REPORTING)\nDet_ReportError\nDet.h\nService to report development errors.\nFr_AllSlots\nFr.h\nInvokes the CC CHI command ’ALL_SLOTS’.\nFr_CancelTxLPdu\nFr.h\nCancels the already pending transmission of a LPdu\ncontained in a controllers physical transmit resource\n(e.g. message buffer).\nFr_DisableLPdu\nFr.h\nDisables the hardware resource of a LPdu for\ntransmission/reception.\nFr_GetChannelStatus\nFr.h\nGets the channel status information.\nFr_GetClockCorrection\nFr.h\nGets the current clock correction values. See\nvariables vInterimRateCorrection and vInterimOffset\nCorrection of [12] for details.\nFr_GetNmVector\nFr.h\nGets the network management vector of the last\ncommunication cycle.\nFr_GetNumOfStartupFrames\nFr.h\nGets the current number of startup frames seen on\nthe cluster. See variable vStartupPairs of [12] for\ndetails.\nFr_GetSyncFrameList\nFr.h\nGets a list of syncframes received or transmitted on\nchannel A and channel B via the even and odd\ncommunication cycle. See variables vsSyncIdListA\nand vsSyncIdListB of [12] for details.\nFr_GetWakeupRxStatus\nFr.h\nGets the wakeup received information from the Flex\nRay controller.\n▽\n△\nAPI Function\nHeader File\nDescription\nFr_PrepareLPdu\nFr.h\nPrepares a LPdu.\nFr_ReadCCConfig\nFr.h\nReads a FlexRay protocol configuration parameter\nfor a particular FlexRay controller out of the\nmodule’s configuration.\nFr_ReconfigLPdu\nFr.h\nReconfigures a given LPdu according to the\nparameters (FrameId, Channel, CycleRepetition,\nCycleOffset, PayloadLength, HeaderCRC) at\nruntime.\nFrTrcv_DisableTransceiverBranch\nFrTrcv.h\nThis function disables the specified branch on the\naddressed (active star) transceiver.\nFrTrcv_EnableTransceiverBranch\nFrTrcv.h\nThis function enables the specified branch on the\naddressed (active star) transceiver.\nFrTrcv_GetTransceiverError\nFrTrcv.h\nAll mandatory errors defined by the FlexRay EPL [5]\nwhich are supported by the FlexRay transceiver\nhardware can be accessed via this API:In addition to\nerrors on the physical layer and local to the ECU\nhardware, a global error flag is provided.\nLSduR_FrIfRxIndication (draft)\nLSduR_FrIf.h\nIndication of a received PDU from a lower layer\ncommunication interface module.\nLSduR_FrIfTriggerTransmit (draft)\nLSduR_FrIf.h\nWithin this API, the upper layer module (called\nmodule) shall check whether the available data fits\ninto the buffer size reported by PduInfoPtr->Sdu\nLength. If it fits, it shall copy its data into the buffer\nprovided by PduInfoPtr->SduDataPtr and update the\nlength of the actual copied data in PduInfoPtr->Sdu\nLength. If not, it returns E_NOT_OK without\nchanging PduInfoPtr.\nLSduR_FrIfTxConfirmation (draft)\nLSduR_FrIf.h\nThe lower layer communication interface module\nconfirms the transmission of a PDU, or the failure to\ntransmit a PDU.\nMirror_ReportFlexRayFrame\nMirror.h\nReports a received or transmitted FlexRay frame or\na Tx conflict.\n⌋"

      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.2: CC Indexing Scheme of the FlexRay Interface [SWS_FrIf_05060] Upstream requirements: SRS_Fr_05096 ⌈In order to abstract for upper layer BSW modules the various CCs, which the FrIf module controls via the FlexRay Driver modules, the FrIf module offers an abstract, unique, zero-based consecutive index FrIfCtrlIdx as configuration parameter, which maps to a tuple of FlexRay Driver API Service function pointer and CC index Fr_Ctrl Idx.⌋"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_FRIF_FIGURE_Figure_7_3_FLEXRAYINTERFACE",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_FlexRayInterface",
      "source_page": 23,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.98,
      "disposition": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "verified",
      "guideline": "Normativ verbindlicher Beleg (🔒 Verifizierter Kontext)",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.3: Flexray Transceiver Indexing Scheme of the FlexRay Interface In order to abstract for upper layer BSW modules the various FlexRay T ransceiver modules, which the FrIf module accesses via the FlexRay T ransceiver Driver modules, the FrIf module takes advantage of the fact that each FlexRay T ransceiver module is unambiguously assigned to a specific Channel on a specific FlexRay CC. Therefore, the FrIf module abstracts the various FlexRay T ransceivers by a combination of the two indices FrIf_CtrlIdx (Controller Index) and FrIf_ChnlIdx (Channel Index) and maps this to a tuple of FlexRay T ransceiver Driver API Service function pointer and FlexRay T ransceiver index FrT rcv_T rcvIdx. (T ransceiver Index) The function descriptions in Chapter 8 specify the required mapping of upper layer BSW module’s parameters to corresponding lower layer BSW module’s API services in detail.\" [SWS_FrIf_05107] Upstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00162 ⌈Besides hardware and software resources, the FrIf module also numbers the logical structure elements presented by FlexRay with an abstract, unique, zero-based consec- utive index. The static configuration data of the FrIf module contains a data structure that specifies which FlexRay CC modules and which FlexRay T ransceiver modules are connected to which Clusters, or in other words, that maps each value of FrIf_ClstIdx to (one, or in general) a set of values for FrIf_CtrlIdx and tuples of (FrIfCtrlIIdx, FrIf_ChnlIdx). ⌋"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_FRIF_FIGURE_Figure_7_3_FLEXRAYNETWORKMANAGEMENT",

      "source_page": 40,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.98,
      "disposition": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "verified",
      "guideline": "Normativ verbindlicher Beleg (🔒 Verifizierter Kontext)",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.3: FlexRay NM Mainfunction Execution Note: The time duration denoted as FrIf RX-Time is the time duration between the end of transmission of the FlexRay frame till the call to FrNm_RxIndication by the FlexRay Interface (FrIf) via the L-SDU Router (LSduR). The time duration denoted as FrIf TX-Time is the time duration between the FrNm’s call to FrIf_Transmit via the L-SDU Router (LSduR) till the start of the transmission of the corresponding frame."
    },

      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.4: FlexRay Interface State Machine State Description FRIF_ST A TE_OFFLINE No communication services are executed (see Chapter 7.6 for details) FRIF_ST A TE_ONLINE All communication services (reception, transmission, transmission confirmation) are executed (see Chapter 7.6 for details). Table 7.1: FlexRay State Machine Transitions (1) [SWS_FrIf_05117] Upstream requirements: SRS_Fr_05031 ⌈During initialization of the FrIf by executing FrIf_Init() the FrIf_State for each cluster shall be initialized with state ’FRIF_ST A TE_OFFLINE’. The transitions are requested by an API service FrIf_SetState() which takes the Cluster to process on and the T ransistion name to invoke. ⌋ [SWS_FrIf_05118] ⌈If the FrIf module’s environment calls the function FrIf_SetState with parameter FrIf_StateT ransition = FRIF_GOTO_ONLINE and if the current state for the requested cluster is FRIF_ST A TE_OFFLINE, the FrIf module shall take the current state of the requested cluster to FRIF_ST A TE_ONLINE.\". If the FrIf module’s environment calls the function FrIf_SetState with parameter FrIf_ StateT ransition = FRIF_GOTO_ OFFLINE and if the current state for the requested cluster is FRIF_ST A TE_ONLINE, the FrIf module shall take the current state of the requested cluster to FRIF_ST A TE_OFFLINE.\". Otherwise, do not perform a state transition. ⌋ For details see Figure 7.4 and T able 7.2 T ransition Name T ransitions (see Figure 7.4) Description FRIF_GOTO_ONLINE (2) T ransition resulting in FrIf_State FRIF_ ST A TE_ONLINE FRIF_GOTO_OFFLINE (3) T ransition resulting in FrIf_State FRIF_ ST A TE_OFFLINE Table 7.2: FlexRay State Machine Transitions (2)"
    },

    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_FRIF_SECTION_12_6_Migration_from_OIL_to_XML",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_OS",
      "source_page": 403,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "12.6 Migration from OIL to XML\nThis version of the AUTOSAR OS specification does not directly support the config-\nuration via OIL. The support for OIL was dropped in favour of XML because XML is\nthe standard configuration language in AUTOSAR and is essential if configuration data\nhas to be imported / exported from / to other AUTOSAR modules or between different\ntools during development.\nSince OIL and XML are both ASCII formats a tool vendor may offer a possibility to\nimport (old) OIL files and to store them as (AUTOSAR OS) XML files. Currently all\nknown vendors support at least the import of existing OIL configurations.\nNote that for showing conformance to the OSEK OS specification, each OSEK OS ven-\ndor must support OIL. This means that practically each AUTOSAR OS vendor will offer\nsome sort of import of OIL configurations - at least to show the OSEK OS conformance."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_FRIF_SECTION_12_8_Integration_hints_for_peripheral_protection",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_OS",
      "source_page": 404,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "12.8 Integration hints for peripheral protection\nPeripheral protection requires configuration on the core level usually conditioned by a\nsupervisor access. For this reason the task of the peripheral protection is assigned to\nthe OS module.\nPeripheral protection may be implemented in two ways\n- using MPU\n- using dedicated peripheral protection units of the target MCU.\nWhen using the memory protection unit, it is reasonable if two or more protected region\ndescriptors are available for peripheral protection mechanism. The region descriptors\nshall be programmed to allow access to those peripherals the current OS-Application\nshall work with. The defined regions shall cover all memory mapped configuration\nregisters for the periphiherals to be protected. The advantage of using the MPU is that\nthe configuration is the same as for memory protection. One of the disadvantages of\nthis method is that it could be impossilbe to cover all peripheral control registers with\navailable MPU region descriptors. The number of such descriptors is typically low.\nBeware that using this method may have implication to the linker file of the project\nsoftware configuration.\nSecond method is using a dedicated register protection schema. This method shall\nallow to precisely select peripherals for every OS Application. However the number of\nperipherals may make the register protection implementation rather bulky. Therefore it\nis advisable to reduce the number of protected peripherals to a reasonable value.\nFor both methods the configuration shall be placed into custom OS Application prop-\nerties. The configuration shall be active when a Task (or ISR) of a particular OS\nApplication is running."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_FRIF_SECTION_12_9_Termination_of_OS_Applications",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_OS",
      "source_page": 328,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "12.9 Termination of OS-Applications\nInconsistencies may occur when an OsApplication is terminated and restarted, de-\npending on its state at the termination.\n• A notification from an asynchronous job started before the termination of OsAp-\nplication can occur after the restart of OsApplication.\n• An asynchronous memory read or write started before the termination of OsAp-\nplication can occur after restart, and cause data inconsistency.\n• A requested mode or state to another OsApplication (e.g. from a SW-C to\nA BSW) can lead to unsynchronized state machines after an OsApplication\nrestart.\nTherefore some measures shall be taken to avoid these inconsistencies and guaranty\na correct behavior.\nIntegration code shall stop all signals and signalgroups during its OsApplication\nrestart. This ensures that no late asynchronous notification will occur after the OsAp-\nplication restart. These signals and signalgroups can be then safely restarted if\nneeded.\nA SW-C shall cancel jobs on all its memory blocks with a call to NvM_CancelJobs\nduring the restart of its OsApplication. As the job might have already been started,\nthe call to NvM_CancelJobs can return an error; in that case, the OsApplication\nshall wait until end of the job to continue. After all jobs are ensured to be cancelled, then\nall memory blocks shall be reset to their initial value, in order to avoid inconsistency of\ndata which might have been written before the cancellation.\nAny SW-C having responsible for requesting mode or state to BSW mode managers\nshall always request a default mode upon a restart of its OsApplication. Thus the\nBSW mode manager would not be stuck into a mode previously requested by the\nOsApplication before its termination. To support this task, note that RTE offers\nmechanisms to handle partition stop and restart wrt. mode machines. For mode man-\nagers an \"error mode\" to be set by RTE can be identified. For mode user partition\nthe behaviour can also be selected. Furthermore an interaction to BswM to trigger an\naction list in case of partition restart can be initiated. Refer to RTE specification for\ndetails.\nAs a global hint, in any non-trusted OsApplication, which could be terminated, there\nshall always be a restart Task which does the following actions:\n• Cancel all jobs which can result in an asynchronous notification or shared mem-\nory, I/O access.\n• Reset all shared memory with a default value.\n• Reset any mode or state residing in another OsApplication and controlled by\nthis given OsApplication to a default value.\nPlease note that some of these actions need to be performed even if an OS-Application\nis merely terminated and not restarted. For example, it may still be necessary to stop\nall signals and signal groups used by the OsApplication. Otherwise, it may happen\nthat a bus never goes to sleep.\nConsequently, in such a case it is necessary to activate the restart Task to perform\nthe necessary cleanup even if the OS-Application is only terminated and not restarted.\nCalling TerminateApplication(<ownappid>,OS_OSAPPLICATION_NO_RESTART)\nin the restart Task will finally set the OS-Application to APPLICATION_TERMINATED."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_FRIF_SECTION_14_The_available_data_length_evaluation_depends_on_different_scenarios_the_FrTp_is_used_in",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_FlexRayISOTransportLayer",
      "source_page": 46,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "14  The available data length evaluation depends on different scenarios the FrTp is used in.\n- In case of a normal ECU which transfers data with unknown message lengths it is necessary to\nevaluate the length of the currently stored FrTp-N-SDU.\n- In case an ECU transmits data with known message length the Tx data length is given by the\nparameter of the FrTp_Transmit service primitive. An additional evaluation by calling\nPduR_FrTpCopyTxData(..) is possible to have equal evaluation sequences for known and\nunknown message length transfers but could be skipped by runtime optimisation (implementation\ndependency).\n- In case of a Gateway which routes N-SDUs of different bus systems it is necessary to get the\ncurrently available (received) data length in the gateway buffer.\n[SWS_FrTp_01048]\n⌈The FrTp module shall decide whether segmentation for\nthe requested N-SDU transfer is required or not depending on the\nlength information of the first allocated FrTpTxPdu from an\nFrTpTxPduPool for the currently processed FrTpConnection (see\nalso Diagram 2). ⌋()\nFrTpTxSdu.Length >\n( FrTpTxPdu.Length -\nAI.Length - PCI.Length )\nInitial processing of FrTpTxSdu\nSegmentation is required\nSegmentation is not required\nyes\nno\nDiagram 2:  Segmentation decision\nNote:\nThe decision whether segmentation is possible or not depends also on\nthe connection mode (1:1 or 1:n).\n[SWS_FrTp_01123]\n⌈The FrTp module shall call the service primitive\nPduR_FrTpCopyTxData() to copy the currently available FrTp N-\nSDU data with a length of FrTpTxPdu length to the corresponding\ntransmit buffer.⌋()\n[SWS_FrTp_01049]\n⌈The FrTp module shall prepare the Address Information\nand PCI according to the result of [SWS_FrTp_01048 as defined in\nspecification ISO 10681-2 [16].⌋()\n[SWS_FrTp_01050]\n⌈The FrTp module shall initiate an N-PDU data transfer by\ncalling the service primitive FrIf_Transmit() with the TxPduId of the\nrecently allocated FrTpTxPdu.⌋()\n[SWS_FrTp_01051]\n⌈The FrTp shall set the corresponding data length\nreferenced by the service primitive FrIf_Transmit’s parameter\nPduInfoType to the exact data length of the buffer15.⌋()"

position outside the buffer of the sender, then\nthe FrTp module shall abort the transmission of this message and The time duration denoted as\nFrIf TX-Time is the time duration between the FrNm’s call to FrIf_Transmit via the\nL-SDU Router (LSduR) till the start of the transmission of the corresponding frame.\n7.7.1\nFlexRay NM-Main Function structure\nThe FlexRay NM MainFunction will hold the \"automated\" functionality of the FlexRay\nNM - as there is the periodic transmission of NM-Messages, the processing of received\nNM-Messages and the periodic processing of the FlexRay NM state machine (at the\nboundary between two NM-Repetition Cycles).\n[SWS_FrNm_00010] ⌈The FrNm module shall call LSduR_FrNmTransmit, which re-\nsults in a call of the FlexRay Interface function FrIf_Transmit, to transmit NM-Vote\nand NM-Data if the transmission of cyclic NM-messages is started.⌋\nNote: The FlexRay Interface module calls LSduR_FrIfTxConfirmation, which in\nturn calls the FrNm module function FrNm_TxConfirmation with E_OK, when a NM-\nmessage is successfully transmitted and a transmit confirmation is supported and con-\nfigured within the FlexRay Interface."

      "verbatim_text": "System Template\n△\nPrecompile time switch to enable the dynamic PNC-to-channel-mapping handling.\nFalse: Dynamic PNC-to-channel-mapping is disabled\nTrue: Dynamic PNC-to-channel-mapping is enabled\nTemplate Description\nDefines if this EcuInstance shall implement the dynamic PNC-to-channel-mapping functionality on this Communication\nConnector and its respective PhysicalChannel.\nM2 Parameter\nCommunicationConnector.dynamicPncToChannelMappingEnabled\nMapping Rule\nMapping Type\nIf at least one dynamicPncToChannelMappingEnabled attribute is defined and if at least one\nCommunicationConnector of the EcuInstance has dynamicPncToChannelMappingEnabled set to\ntrue, then FrNmDynamicPncToChannelMappingSupport shall be set to true. Otherwise FrNm\nDynamicPncToChannelMappingSupport shall be set to false.\nfull\nMapping Status\nECUC Parameter ID\nvalid\n[ECUC_FrNm_00090]\nBSW Module\nBSW Context\nFrNm\nFrNm/FrNmGlobalConfig/FrNmGlobalFeatures\nBSW Parameter\nBSW Type\nFrNmHwVoteEnable\nECUC-BOOLEAN-PARAM-DEF\nBSW Description\nPre-processor switch for enabling the processing of FlexRay Hardware aggregated NM-Votes. This switch enables/disables\nthe optional API FrIf_GetNmVector.\nTemplate Description\nSwitch for enabling the processing of FlexRay Hardware aggregated NM-Votes.\nM2 Parameter\nFlexrayNmEcu.nmHwVoteEnabled\nMapping Rule\nMapping Type\n1:1 mapping\nfull\nMapping Status\nECUC Parameter ID\nvalid\n[ECUC_FrNm_00050]\nBSW Module\nBSW Context\nFrNm\nFrNm/FrNmGlobalConfig/FrNmGlobalFeatures\nBSW Parameter\nBSW Type\nFrNmPassiveModeEnabled\nECUC-BOOLEAN-PARAM-DEF\nBSW Description\nPre-processor switch for enabling Passive Node Configuration support.\nTemplate Description\nEnables support of the Passive Mode. The passive mode is configurable per channel.\nM2 Parameter\nNmNode.nmPassiveModeEnabled\nMapping Rule\nMapping Type\n1:1 mapping. nmNode.nmPassiveModeEnabled shall always have the same value in all Nm\nClusters with the same bus protocol in the scope of one EcuInstance.\nfull\nMapping Status\nECUC Parameter ID\nvalid\n[ECUC_FrNm_00043]"

      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_FRIF_SECTION_2_4_4_API_Function_Parameters",
      "source_element": null,

      "source_page": 20,

      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "2.4.4 API Function Parameters\n[TR_BSWMG_00020] API Function Parameters ⌈The function parameters shall have\nmandatory entries for “Name”, “Type”, “Direction” and “Notes”.⌋()\n[TR_BSWMG_00032] API Function Parameter types ⌈The parameter “Type” shall be\none of the existing types defined in the BSW model.⌋()\n[TR_BSWMG_00033] C-Style Pointers as API Function Parameters ⌈Parameters\nmay be modeled as C-Style pointers by appending * to the parameter type, e.g.\nPduInfoType*⌋()\n[TR_BSWMG_00027] Mandatory pointers for API Function Output Parameters\n⌈Parameters must be modeled as pointers if their “Direction” attribute is set to out or\ninout.⌋()\n[TR_BSWMG_00035] Mandatory constant types for pointers of API Function In-\nput Parameters ⌈Pointer-type parameters of direction type “in\", i.e. parameters that\nrepresent read-only structures or arrays, may prepend the parameter type with the\nconst keyword. This enforces that the data pointed to by the parameter is read-only\nand will not be altered by the function. Example: const FrIf_ConfigType*⌋()\n[TR_BSWMG_00021] API Function Parameter Direction ⌈The parameter’s direction\ntype attribute shall be set to one of the values in, out, inout, return.⌋()\n[TR_BSWMG_00022] API Function Parameter Description ⌈Each parameter shall\nprovide a short description about its purpose.⌋()\nNote: EA provides a textfield called ‘Notes’ to take the parameters description.\n[TR_BSWMG_00023] API Function Return Parameter ⌈If the function’s return type\nis not equal to void, the return value shall be modeled like an operation parameter\nwith the following exceptions: It shall be the first parameter in the list. Additionally, it\nshall be the only parameter to have its “Direction” set to “return”. The notes field shall\nconcisely describe the possible return values.⌋()\nModeling Guidelines of Basic Software EA UML\nModel\nFigure 2.5: Parameter example of a API function\n[TR_BSWMG_00922] API Function Return Value Links ⌈All possible return values\nfor an API function’s return parameter that are described in the notes field of the pa-\nrameter shall be linked to the definition of the value.\nIn particular, if the function’s return type is a simple type (see [TR_BSWMG_00066])\nthe link shall be put as\n[ARDataTypeElement{<AttributeName>}{<DataTypeName>}].\nIf it is an enumeration (see [TR_BSWMG_00072]) the link shall be put as\n[AREnumLiteral{<LiteralName>}{<DataTypeName>}].\nNote\nthat\n<DataTypeName>\nshall\nbe\nset\nto\nthe\nanchor\nname\n(see\n[TR_BSWMG_00031]) of the datatype if one is defined.⌋()\nExample: The correct way to link the return values in the example of Figure 2.5 is to\nput this description into the notes field of the return parameter:\n[ARDataTypeElement{E_OK}{Std_ReturnType}]: Cancellation of request timeout was successful<br/>\n[ARDataTypeElement{E_NOT_OK}{Std_ReturnType}]: Cancellation of request timeout was not\nsuccessful\nNote: If the return type has an extension (as defined in 2.4.8.3) then always the type\nin the model defining the current value has to be linked.\nExample: If an API function in the Csm module returns the Std_ReturnType then e.g.\nvalues E_OK and CRYPTO_E_BUSY may be returned as the latter value is defined\nin Csm_ReturnType, which is an extension to Std_ReturnType. In that case the links\nhave to be set like this:\n[ARDataTypeElement{E_OK}{Std_ReturnType}]: ...<br/>\n[ARDataTypeElement{CRYPTO_E_BUSY}{Csm_ReturnType}]: ...\nModeling Guidelines of Basic Software EA UML\nModel\n[TR_BSWMG_00129] Optional Parameters of API Functions ⌈The existence of a\nparameter may depend on the module configuration. In this case, the parameter shall\nhave the stereotype ≪optional≫.⌋()\n[TR_BSWMG_00130] Multiplicity of API Function Parameters ⌈A parameter with a\ngiven type may occur several times, where the multiplicity is specified by configuration.\nIn this case, the parameter shall have the stereotype ≪multiple≫.⌋()\nHint: Don’t use the multiplicity button in the parameter edit mask to configure the mul-\ntiplicity.\n[TR_BSWMG_00131] Mutual Exclusive Variants of API Function Parameters ⌈A\nparameter may appear in different variants within the same position of the function\nsignature, where one specific variant will be selected by configuration. In this case, the\nparameter shall be modeled several times in all its possible variants and each variant\nof the parameter shall have the stereotype ≪mutualexcl≫.⌋()\nExample: The parameter “buffer” of the Xfrm function “<Mip>_<transformerId>” can\nbe configured either as “inout” or “out”. It therefore shall be modeled two times, one\ntime with Direction “inout” and the second time with Direction “out”. Since Enterprise\nArchitect requires parameter names to be unique, the first parameter variant may be\nnamed “buffer{inout}” and the second one “buffer{out}”.\nHint: All variants of a mutual exclusive parameter shall have the same name; the name\nwithout the curly brackets (including the text) have to be the same.\nFigure 2.6: Mutual Exclusive Parameter example of a API function\nModeling Guidelines of Basic Software EA UML\nModel"

      "source_element": null,

      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "5.2 FlexRay Interface\nThe following services of the FlexRay Interface are called by the FlexRay AUTOSAR\nTransport Layer module:\n FrIf_Transmit\nBy this API service, the sending of a frame (N-PDU) is triggered. Depending\non configuration on the FlexRay Interface, the N-PDU is sent immediately or\nafter the call of FrArTp_TriggerTransmit.\nThe following services of the FlexRay AUTOSAR Transport Layer module are called\nby the FlexRay Interface:\n FrArTp_RxIndication\nBy this API service, the FlexRay Interface indicates the reception of an FrArTp\nframe (N-PDU, please do not mistake this with a FlexRay frame) to the\nFrArTp. The FrArTp then processes this frame.\n FrArTp_TxConfirmation\nBy this API service, the FlexRay Interface confirms the (un)successful sending\nof the frame containing the N-PDU over the FlexRay network.\n FrArTp_TriggerTransmit\nBy this API service, the FlexRay Interface makes the FrArTp to copy the N-\nPDU into the buffer provided by the FlexRay Interface. The FlexRay interface\nthen can start sending the FlexRay frame containing the N-PDU."

      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "5.3 FlexRay Interface\nThe following services primitives of the FlexRay Interface (FrIf) module are called by\nthe FrTp:\n FrIf_Transmit\nBy this API service primitive, the transfer of an Fr N-PDU is initiated.\nThe following services primitives of the FrTp module are called by the FlexRay\nInterface module:\n FrTp_RxIndication\nBy this API service primitive, the FlexRay Interface module indicates the\nreception of an FrTp frame (Fr N-PDU, not to be confused with a FlexRay\nframe) to the FrTp. The FrTp then processes this frame.\n FrTp_TxConfirmation\nBy this API service primitive, the FlexRay Interface module confirms the\nsending of the frame containing the Fr N-PDU with result (E_OK if the\ntransmission was successful, E_NOT_OK if the transmission failed) over the\nFlexRay network.\n FrTp_TriggerTransmit\nBy this API service primitive, the FlexRay Interface get access to the Fr N-\nPDU data.1"
    },

Receiving and transmitting messages\n• FrIf - Accessing the clock unit in the FlexRay controller\n• BswM - Coordination of network access (via FrTSyn_SetTransmissionMode)\n• Det - Reporting of development errors\n• IdsM -       "verbatim_text": "5 Dependencies to other modules\nThe PDU Router module depends on the APIs and capabilities of the used communi-\ncation hardware abstraction layer modules and the used communication service layer\nmodules. Basically the API functions required by the PDU Router module are:\nCommunication Interface modules:\n• <Lo>_Transmit (e.g. CanIf_Transmit, FrIf_Transmit, LinIf_Trans-\nmit)\n• <Lo>_CancelTransmit (e.g. FrIf_CancelTransmit)\nTransport Protocol Modules:\n• <LoTp>_Transmit (e.g.\nCanTp_Transmit,\nFrTp_Transmit,\nLinTp_\nTransmit)\n• <LoTp>_CancelTransmit (e.g.\nCanTp_CancelTransmit, FrTp_Cancel\nTransmit)\n• <LoTp>_CancelReceive (e.g. CanTp_CancelReceive, FrTp_CancelRe-\nceive)\nUpper layer modules which use Transport Protocol modules:\n• <Up>_StartOfReception (e.g. Dcm_StartOfReception)\n• <Up>_CopyRxData (e.g. Dcm_CopyRxData)\n• <Up>_CopyTxData (e.g. Dcm_CopyTxData)\n• <Up>_TpRxIndication (e.g. Dcm_TpRxIndication)\n• <Up>_TpTxConfirmation (e.g. Dcm_TpTxConfirmation)\nUpper layer modules which process I-PDUs originating from Communication Interface\nmodules:\n• <Up>_RxIndication (e.g. Com_RxIndication),\n• <Up>_TxConfirmation (e.g. Com_TxConfirmation),\n• <Up>_TriggerTransmit (e.g. Com_TriggerTransmit)"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "7.3.1 FlexRay Interface Main Function\nThe FlexRay Interface Main Function needs to be called cyclically from a task body pro-\nvided by the BSW Scheduler with a calling period (FRIF_MAINFUNCTION_PERIOD)\ndepending on the FlexRay Cycle length and configurable at system configuration time.\nSince the Cycle length of each Cluster is independent, the desired calling period of\nthe FlexRay Interface Main Function might differ from Cluster to Cluster, except for\n\"Transmission with Immediate Buffer Access\".\n[SWS_FrIf_05119]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00432\n⌈The FrIf module shall provide one dedicated FlexRay Interface Main Function for each\nFlexRay Cluster that is controlled by that FrIf module.⌋\n[SWS_FrIf_05283]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00373\n⌈The API names of the FlexRay Interface Main Functions shall obey the following pat-\ntern:\nFrIf_MainFunction_<FrIfCluster.ShortName>\nwhere\nFrIfCluster.ShortName\nis\nthe\nShort Name of the corresponding FrIfCluster.⌋\n[SWS_FrIf_15120] ⌈The Main Function monitors and controls the continuous execu-\ntion of the FlexRay Job List Execution Function including the (re)synchronization if the\ncurrent FlexRay Interface State Machine is FRIF_STATE_ONLINE.⌋\n[SWS_FrIf_01124] ⌈If Bus Mirroring is enabled globally (see FrIfBusMirroringSupport),\nthen call Fr_GetChannelStatus for all controllers of each FlexRay cluster for which mir-\nroring has been activated with a call to FrIf_EnableBusMirroring(), merge the states\nreported for the controllers of one cluster with a binary OR, and then call Mirror_Re-\nportFlexRayChannelStatus() with the cluster, Fr_ChannelAStatusPtr, and Fr_Channel\nBStatusPtr to report the aggregated channel states to the Bus Mirroring module.⌋\n[SWS_FrIf_25120] ⌈If one of the optional cluster-specific configuration parameters\nFRIF_E_NIT_CH_A, FRIF_E_NIT_CH_B, FRIF_E_SW_CH_A, FRIF_E_SW_CH_B or\nFRIF_E_ACS_CH_A, FRIF_E_ACS_CH_B exists, then call FrIf_GetChannelStatus for\neach FlexRay controller of the cluster and report the status to DEM as described be-\nlow.⌋\n[SWS_FrIf_35120] ⌈If the optional configuration parameter FRIF_E_NIT_CH_A ex-\nists, then the channel status information shall be reported to DEM as Dem_Set\nEventStatus (FRIF_E_NIT_CH_A, DEM_EVENT_STATUS_PREFAILED) when any of\nthe error bits of a single controller (Channel A NIT status data vSS!SyntaxError, v\nSS!Bviolation) is set or as Dem_SetEventStatus (FRIF_E_NIT_CH_A, DEM_EVENT_\nSTATUS_PREPASSED) when none of these error bits is set.⌋\n[SWS_FrIf_45120] ⌈If the optional configuration parameter FRIF_E_NIT_CH_B ex-\nists, then the channel status information shall be reported to DEM as Dem_Set\nEventStatus (FRIF_E_NIT_CH_B, DEM_EVENT_STATUS_PREFAILED) when any of\nthe error bits of a single controller (Channel B NIT status data vSS!SyntaxError, v\nSS!Bviolation) is set or as Dem_SetEventStatus (FRIF_E_NIT_CH_B, DEM_EVENT_\nSTATUS_PREPASSED) when none of these error bits is set.⌋\n[SWS_FrIf_55120] ⌈If the optional configuration parameter FRIF_E_SW_CH_A exists,\nthen the channel status information shall be reported to DEM as Dem_SetEventSta-\ntus (FRIF_E_SW_CH_A, DEM_EVENT_STATUS_PREFAILED) when any of the error\nbits of a single controller (Channel A symbol window status data vSS!SyntaxError, v\nSS!Bviolation, vSS!TxConflict) is set or as Dem_SetEventStatus (FRIF_E_SW_CH_A,\nDEM_EVENT_STATUS_PREPASSED) when none of these error bits is set.⌋\n[SWS_FrIf_65120] ⌈If the optional configuration parameter FRIF_E_SW_CH_B exists,\nthen the channel status information shall be reported to DEM as Dem_SetEventSta-\ntus (FRIF_E_SW_CH_B, DEM_EVENT_STATUS_PREFAILED) when any of the error\nbits of a single controller (Channel B symbol window status data vSS!SyntaxError, v\nSS!Bviolation vSS!TxConflict) is set or as Dem_SetEventStatus (FRIF_E_SW_CH_B,\nDEM_EVENT_STATUS_PREPASSED) when none of these error bits is set.⌋\n[SWS_FrIf_75120] ⌈If the optional configuration parameter FRIF_E_ACS_CH_A ex-\nists, then the channel status information shall be reported to DEM as Dem_SetEvent\nStatus (FRIF_E_ACS_CH_A , DEM_EVENT_STATUS_PREFAILED) when any of the\nerror bits of a single controller (Channel A aggregated channel status vSS!SyntaxEr-\nror, vSS!ContentError, vSS!Bviolation, vSS!TxConflict) is set or as Dem_SetEventSta-\ntus (FRIF_E_ACS_CH_A, DEM_EVENT_STATUS_PREPASSED) when none of these\nerror bits is set.⌋\n[SWS_FrIf_85120] ⌈If the optional configuration parameter FRIF_E_ACS_CH_B ex-\nists, then the channel status information shall be reported to DEM as Dem_SetEvent\nStatus (FRIF_E_ACS_CH_B, DEM_EVENT_STATUS_PREFAILED) when any of the\nerror bits of a single controller (Channel B aggregated channel status vSS!SyntaxEr-\nror, vSS!ContentError, vSS!Bviolation, vSS!TxConflict) is set or as Dem_SetEventSta-\ntus (FRIF_E_ACS_CH_B, DEM_EVENT_STATUS_PREPASSED) when none of these\nerror bits is set.⌋\n[SWS_FrIf_95120] ⌈If a loss of the JobList’s synchronization (see JobListAsyncFlag)\nor a miss of execution was detected, the following steps shall be Get the global time (FrIf_GetGlobalTime())\n• If FrIf_GetGlobalTime() returns E_NOT_OK, stop here\n• If FrIf_GetGlobalTime() returns E_OK, continue with step 2\n2. add some ’time buffer’ (i.e. some timespan which takes jitter into account)\n3. search the FlexRay Job List for the next job, i.e. that job with an invocation time\ngreater than the current global time + ’time buffer’.\n4. set the JobListPointer to that job and program the absolute timer with this job’s\ninvocation time (now the FlexRay Job List is synchronized again)\n5. clear the JobListAsyncFlag\n6. Enable the absolute timer interrupt\n⌋"

      "verbatim_text": "7.3.3.1 FlexRay Source Bus Activation\nAfter initialization, the FlexRay Interface module does not report any frames to the Bus\nMirroring module.\n[SWS_Mirror_00036]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Mirror_00010\n⌈When\nMirror_StartSourceNetwork\nis\ncalled\nto\nstart\na\nFlexRay\nsource\nbus,\nthe\nBus\nMirroring\nmodule\nshall\ncall\nFrIf_EnableBusMirroring\nwith\nFrIf_MirroringActive set to TRUE to start reporting of received and transmitted\nFlexRay frames from the corresponding FlexRay cluster.⌋\nMirror_StartSourceNetwork receives a ComMChannelId as network, while\nFrIf_EnableBusMirroring expects a FrIfClstIdx as FrIf_ClstIdx.\nThe\ntranslation of the one to the other can be determined at generation time by following\nthe references from the ComMChannelId to the the related FrIfClstIdx through the\nECU configuration.\n[SWS_Mirror_00037]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Mirror_00010\n⌈When\nMirror_StopSourceNetwork\nis\ncalled\nto\nstop\na\nFlexRay\nsource\nbus,\nthe\nBus\nMirroring\nmodule\nshall\ncall\nFrIf_EnableBusMirroring\nwith\nFrIf_MirroringActive set to FALSE to stop reporting of received and transmit-\nted FlexRay frames from the corresponding FlexRay cluster.⌋"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_FRIF_SECTION_7_3_3_2_FlexRay_Frame_Acquisition",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_BusMirroring",
      "source_page": 33,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "7.3.3.2 FlexRay Frame Acquisition\nThe FlexRay Interface module reports both received and transmitted FlexRay\nframes with a call to Mirror_ReportFlexRayFrame.\nReceived and transmitted\nframes are reported from the job list execution function or the transmit function of the\nFlexRay Interface.\n[SWS_Mirror_00169]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00459\n⌈The Bus Mirroring module shall apply appropriate mechanisms to allow calls of\nMirror_ReportFlexRayFrame from the partition to which the ComMChannel refer-\nenced by MirrorComMNetworkHandleRef is assigned to, e.g. by providing a satel-\nlite in this partition.⌋\nFor each reported FlexRay frame, the FlexRay Interface module provides infor-\nmation about the receiving FlexRay controller and about the slot ID and cycle, the\nlength and the actual payload of the frame, and information about transmission con-\nflicts.\n[SWS_Mirror_00038]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Mirror_00006, SRS_Mirror_00007\n⌈When Mirror_ReportFlexRayFrame is called to report a received or transmit-\nted FlexRay frame (txConflict is reported as FALSE), the Bus Mirroring module\nshall match the slotId and cycle against all active statically configured and dynam-\nically added filters of the corresponding source bus. If the FlexRay frame matches\nat least one filter, it is accepted by the Bus Mirroring module.⌋\nOn the destination bus, the source bus is identified by a network ID, but\nMirror_ReportFlexRayFrame reports the controllerId. The translation of the\none to the other can be determined at generation time by following the references\nfrom the FrIfCtrlIdx to the MirrorNetworkId through the ECU configuration via\nMirrorComMNetworkHandleRef."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_FRIF_SECTION_7_3_3_3_FlexRay_Frame_Filters",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_BusMirroring",
      "source_page": 34,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "7.3.3.3 FlexRay Frame Filters\n[SWS_Mirror_00039]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Mirror_00007\n⌈A FlexRay filter statically configured as MirrorSourceFlexRayFilter matches\nthe reported slotId and cycle if the slotId is greater than or equal to the\nMirrorSourceFlexRayFilterLowerSlot and smaller than or equal to the Mir-\nrorSourceFlexRayFilterUpperSlot and if the cycle modulo MirrorSource-\nFlexRayFilterCycleRepetition is greater than or equal to the MirrorSource-\nFlexRayFilterLowerBaseCycle and smaller than or equal to the Mirror-\nSourceFlexRayFilterUpperBaseCycle.⌋\n[SWS_Mirror_00040]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Mirror_00007\n⌈A FlexRay filter dynamically added by a call to Mirror_AddFlexRayFilter\nmatches the reported slotId and cycle if the slotId is greater than or equal to\nthe lowerSlotId and smaller than or equal to the upperSlotId and if the cycle\nmodulo cycleRepetition is greater than or equal to the lowerBaseCycle and\nsmaller than or equal to the upperBaseCycle.⌋"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_FRIF_SECTION_7_3_3_4_FlexRay_Status_Acquisition",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_BusMirroring",
      "source_page": 33,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "7.3.3.4 FlexRay Status Acquisition\n[SWS_Mirror_00041]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Mirror_00008, SRS_Mirror_00009\n⌈When Mirror_ReportFlexRayFrame is called to report a transmission conflict (\ntxConflict is reported as TRUE), the Bus Mirroring module shall match the slotId\nand cycle against all active statically configured and dynamically added filters. If it\nmatches at least one filter, the reported FlexRay source bus state for that frame shall\nbe set to transmission conflict.⌋\nThe callback Mirror_ReportFlexRayFrame reports a controllerId and the API\nFrIf_GetPOCStatus expects a FrIf_CtrlIdx, but a network ID is required to re-\nport the status to the output bus. The translation of the one to the other can be deter-\nmined at generation time by following the references from the FrIfCtrlIdx to the\nMirrorNetworkId through the ECU configuration via MirrorComMNetworkHan-\ndleRef.\n[SWS_Mirror_00146]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Mirror_00008, SRS_Mirror_00009\n⌈When Mirror_ReportFlexRayChannelStatus is called to report the FlexRay\nchannel state, the Bus Mirroring module shall compare the reported states with\nthe previously reported states. It the states differ in Bit 1 (vSS!SyntaxError), Bit 2\n(vSS!ContentError), and/or Bit 4 (vSS!Bviolation), the Bus Mirroring module shall up-\ndate the reported FlexRay source bus state accordingly.⌋\nThe callback Mirror_ReportFlexRayChannelStatus reports a clusterId and\nthe API FrIf_GetState expects a FrIf_ClstIdx, but a network ID is required to\nreport the status to the output bus. The translation of the one to the other can be de-\ntermined at generation time by following the references from the FrIfClstIdx to the\nMirrorNetworkId through the ECU configuration via MirrorComMNetworkHan-\ndleRef.\n[SWS_Mirror_00042]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Mirror_00008, SRS_Mirror_00009\n⌈The Bus Mirroring module shall poll the status of each active FlexRay source bus by\ncyclically calling FrIf_GetState from the Mirror_MainFunction. If the returned\nFrIf_StatePtr is FRIF_STATE_ONLINE, the reported FlexRay source bus state\nshall be set to online, otherwise to offline. If the bus is online, the Bus Mirroring mod-\nule shall also call FrIf_GetPOCStatus for each controller connected to the FlexRay\ncluster. If the returned Fr_POCStateType is FR_POCSTATE_NORMAL_ACTIVE for\nall controllers, the reported source bus state shall be synchronous and normal ac-\ntive; if Fr_POCStateType is FR_POCSTATE_NORMAL_PASSIVE for at least one con-\ntroller, the reported source bus state shall be synchronous but not normal active; if\nFr_POCStateType is in any other state for at least one controller, the reported source\nbus state shall be neither synchronous nor normal active.⌋"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_FRIF_SECTION_7_3_3_Access_to_FlexRay",
      "source_element": null,

      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "7.3.3 Access to FlexRay\nThe Bus Mirroring module accesses the FlexRay bus through the FlexRay Interface\nmodule (FrIf). After the Bus Mirroring module starts the mirroring of a FlexRay bus,\nthe FlexRay Interface module reports received and transmitted FlexRay frames to the\nBus Mirroring module. The FlexRay bus state is polled cyclically from the Mirror_-\nMainFunction. A FlexRay source bus corresponds to a FlexRay cluster, which can\nbe connected to several controllers."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_FRIF_SECTION_7_3_6_Timers",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_FlexRayStateManager",
      "source_page": 21,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "7.3.6 Timers\nThe state machine description uses the following timers for each FlexRay cluster:\nTimer\nDescription\nt1\nThe timer t1 models the delay of clearing the coldstart inhibit mode (i.e. calling FrIf_Allow\nColdstart).\nThe duration of this timer can be statically configured with the configuration parameter Fr\nSMDurationT1.\nt2\nThe timer t2 models the time difference after which the FrSM will repeat the startup of the\nFlexRay cluster.\nThe duration of this timer can be statically configured with the configuration parameter Fr\nSMDurationT2.\nt3\nThe timer t3 supervises the transition to FullCom. The duration of this timer can be statically\nconfigured with the configuration parameter FrSMDurationT3.\nt4\nThe timer t4 ensures that a dual channel node will eventually clear its coldstart inhibit bit and\nbecome a leading coldstarter.\nt_TrcvStdbyDelay\nThe timer t_TrcvStdbyDelay models the time difference after which the FrSM will\nreinitialize the FlexRay communication controllers and set the transceivers into STANDBY\nmode when FlexRay communication is stopped.\nTable 7.7: FrsM timers\n[SWS_FrSM_00142] ⌈If the configuration parameter FrSMDurationT1 is set to 0, timer\nt1 shall not be started. Instead, the call of FrIf_AllowColdstart shall immediately follow\nthe call of FrIf_StartCommunication.⌋\n[SWS_FrSM_00143] ⌈If the duration FrSMDurationT2 of timer t2 is set to 0, the\nstartup of the FlexRay cluster shall not be supervised.\nNote, that no assumption is made whether any of the timers is implemented in software\nor hardware.⌋\n[SWS_FrSM_00209] ⌈If the configuration parameter FrSMTrcvStdbyDelay is not con-\nfigured or set to 0, timer t_TrcvStdbyDelay shall not be started. Instead, the transi-\ntion from state FRSM_HALT_REQ to FRSM_READY shall be executed immediately.⌋"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_FRIF_SECTION_7_3_7_Functional_Elements",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_FlexRayStateManager",
      "source_page": 22,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "7.3.7 Functional Elements\nThe functionality being performed in the transitions of the state machine is partitioned\ninto the following functional elements. I.e. the following table contains abbreviations\nused as actions in the FrSM state machine description, which reference one or more\nfunction calls visible at the interfaces of the FrSM module.\nFunctional Element\nDescription\nFE_WAKEUP\nCall FrIf_SendWUP for each controller of the FlexRay cluster.\nFE_SET_WU_CHANNEL_INITIAL\nIn case of a single channel node, do nothing.\nIn case of a dual channel node, call FrIf_SetWakeupChannel for each\ncontroller of the FlexRay cluster in order to set the wakeup channel to\nthe channel A.\nFE_SET_WU_CHANNEL_FORWARD\nIn case of a single channel node, do nothing.\nIn case of a dual channel node, call FrIf_SetWakeupChannel for each\ncontroller of the FlexRay cluster in order to set the wakeup channel to\nthe channel on which no wakeup has been detected while evaluating\nWUReason.\nFE_CONFIG\nCall FrIf_ControllerInit for each controller of the FlexRay cluster.\nFE_START\nCall FrIf_StartCommunication for each controller of the FlexRay cluster.\nFE_ALLOW_COLDSTART\nCall FrIf_AllowColdstart for each controller of the FlexRay cluster if the\nconfiguration parameter FrSMIsColdstartEcu is true.\nFE_HALT\nCall FrIf_HaltCommunication for each controller of the FlexRay cluster.\nFE_TRCV_STANDBY\nCall FrIf_SetTransceiverMode with FrIf_TrcvMode as FRTRCV_\nTRCVMODE_STANDBY for each transceiver of the FlexRay cluster.\nFE_TRCV_NORMAL\nIn case the FrSM state machine is in state FRSM_ECU_ACTIVE, call Fr\nIf_SetTransceiverMode with FrIf_TrcvMode as FRTRCV_TRCVMODE_\nNORMAL and FrIf_ClearTransceiverWakeup for each transceiver of the\nFlexRay cluster.\nIn case the FrSM state machine is in state FRSM_ECU_PASSIVE, call Fr\nIf_SetTransceiverMode with FrIf_TrcvMode as FRTRCV_TRCVMODE_\nRECEIVEONLY and FrIf_ClearTransceiverWakeup for each transceiver\nof the FlexRay cluster.\nFE_START_FRIF\nSet the FrIf state to ONLINE by calling FrIf_SetState with FrIf_State\nTransition as FRIF_GOTO_ONLINE\nfor the cluster.\nFE_STOP_FRIF\nSet the FrIf state to OFFLINE by calling FrIf_SetState with FrIf_State\nTransition as FRIF_GOTO_OFFLINE for the cluster.\nFE_DEM_STATUS_FAILED\nReport status of production error FRSM_E_CLUSTER_STARTUP as\nfailed.\nFE_DEM_STATUS_PASSED\nReport status of production error FRSM_E_CLUSTER_STARTUP as\npassed.\nFE_DEM_SYNC_LOSS\nReport the status of the production error\nFRSM_E_CLUSTER_SYNC_LOSS as failed. If the name of an indication\nfunction (see Section 8.6.3) is configured, call the indication function\nwith the parameter SyncLossErrorStatus = true.\nFE_DEM_SYNC_LOSS_PASSED\nIf the name of an indication function (see Section 8.6.3) is configured,\ncall the indication function with the parameter SyncLossErrorStatus =\nfalse. Additionally report the status of the production error\nFRSM_E_CLUSTER_SYNC_LOSS as passed.\nFE_FULL_COM_IND\nIndicate to the ComM that FullCom has been reached by calling Com\nM_BusSM_ModeIndication (FullCom)\nFE_NO_COM_IND\nIndicate to the ComM that FullCom has been left by calling ComM_Bus\nSM_ModeIndication (NoCom).\nFE_STARTUP_ERROR_IND\nCall FrNm_StartupError."
    },

      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_FRIF_SECTION_7_3_8_Wakeup_Pattern_Transmission",
      "source_element": null,

      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "7.3.8 Wakeup Pattern Transmission\n[SWS_FrSM_00208] ⌈The FrSM shall repeat the transmission of wakeup patterns ac-\ncording to the configuration parameter FrSMNumWakeupPatterns. I.e. the FlexRay\nState Manager shall perform the following actions while being in state FRSM_WAKEUP:\n• Set counter wakeupCounter to 1 when the state FRSM_WAKEUP is entered\n• While wakeupCounter < FrSMNumWakeupPatterns and busTrafficDe-\ntected = false:\n– Wait until the FlexRay controllers of the FlexRay cluster are in state FR_\nREADY\n– When the FlexRay controllers are in state FR_READY, check vPOC!Wakeup\nStatus of the FlexRay controllers and act as follows:\n* if vPOC!WakeupStatus = FR_WAKEUP_RECEIVED_HEADER ∨FR_\nWAKEUP_RECEIVED_WUP: busTrafficDetected := true\n* else if vPOC!WakeupStatus = FR_WAKEUP_TRANSMITTED: wakeup-\nTransmitted := true\n* else: wakeupTransmitted := false\n• If busTrafficDetected = false and wakeupCounter < FrSMNumWakeup-\nPatterns, execute FE_WAKEUP\n• Increment the wakeupCounter\nIf any of the FlexRay controllers enters the HALT state due to an error condition, the\nwakeup pattern transmission shall be aborted and the wakeupFinished condition\nshall evaluate to true.⌋"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "7.3 FlexRay Interface State Machine\n[SWS_FrIf_05115] ⌈In order to allow to control the communication operations of the\nFlexRay system, the FrIf module shall implement a behavior, which is defined using\na simple state machine (one per FlexRay cluster), called FlexRay Interface State Ma-\nchine⌋\nInitial\nFRIF_STATE_OFFLINE\nFRIF_STATE_ONLINE\n(2)\n(3)\n(1)\nFigure 7.4: FlexRay Interface State Machine\nState\nDescription\nFRIF_STATE_OFFLINE\nNo communication services are executed (see Section 7.6\nfor details)\nFRIF_STATE_ONLINE\nAll communication services (reception, transmission,\ntransmission confirmation) are executed (see Section 7.6 for\ndetails).\nTable 7.1: FlexRay State Machine Transitions (1)\n[SWS_FrIf_05117]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Fr_05031\n⌈During initialization of the FrIf by executing FrIf_Init() the FrIf_State for each cluster\nshall be initialized with state ’FRIF_STATE_OFFLINE’.\nThe transitions are requested by an API service FrIf_SetState() which takes the Cluster\nto process on and the Transistion name to invoke.⌋\n[SWS_FrIf_05118] ⌈If the FrIf module’s environment calls the function FrIf_SetState\nwith parameter FrIf_StateTransition = FRIF_GOTO_ONLINE and if the current state for\nthe requested cluster is FRIF_STATE_OFFLINE, the FrIf module shall take the current\nstate of the requested cluster to FRIF_STATE_ONLINE.\".\nIf the FrIf module’s environment calls the function FrIf_SetState with parameter FrIf_\nStateTransition = FRIF_GOTO_ OFFLINE and if the current state for the requested\ncluster is FRIF_STATE_ONLINE, the FrIf module shall take the current state of the\nrequested cluster to FRIF_STATE_OFFLINE.\".\nOtherwise, do not perform a state transition.⌋\nFor details see Figure 7.4 and Table 7.2\nTransition Name\nTransitions\n(see Figure 7.4)\nDescription\nFRIF_GOTO_ONLINE\n(2)\nTransition resulting in FrIf_State FRIF_\nSTATE_ONLINE\nFRIF_GOTO_OFFLINE\n(3)\nTransition resulting in FrIf_State FRIF_\nSTATE_OFFLINE\nTable 7.2: FlexRay State Machine Transitions (2)\n[SWS_FrIf_05501] ⌈If the API FrIf_SetState with parameter FRIF_STATE_OFFLINE\nis called, the FlexRay Interface module shall check the parameter \"TxConfCounter\"\nfor every PDU. If the value for the corresponding PDU is greater than 0, the FlexRay\nInterface shall call the upper layer using the API LSduR_FrIfConfirmation(id, E_NOT_\nOK).⌋\nNote: It has to be ensured that the FlexRay Interface does not lose the TxConfCounter\nvalues at the point in time the API FrIf_SetState with parameter FRIF_STATE_OF-\nFLINE is called."
    },
