      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_FRTRCV_SECTION_8_3_1_FrTrcv_Init",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_FlexRayTransceiverDriver",

      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "8.3.1 FrTrcv_Init\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00322] Definition of API function FrTrcv_Init ⌈\nService Name\nFrTrcv_Init\nSyntax\nvoid FrTrcv_Init (\nconst FrTrcv_ConfigType* ConfigPtr\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x00\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nNon Reentrant\nParameters (in)\nConfigPtr\nPointer to the selected configuration set.\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nNone\nDescription\nThis service initializes the FrTrcv.\nAvailable via\nFrTrcv.h\n⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00008] Initialization interface\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00101\n⌈The FlexRay transceiver driver initializes variables and hardware resources in a sep-\narate initialization function. This function shall be named FrTrcv_Init().\nNote: According to [SWS_EcuM_02562]: Drivers which serve wakeup sources must be\nre-initialized in the restart block. The driver restart shall re-arm the trigger mechanism\nof the ’wakeup detected’ call-back.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00228] Initialization Sequence for FlexRay Transceiver Driver\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Fr_05134\n⌈The FlexRay Transceiver Driver shall support the configuration sequence of the AU-\nTOSAR stack.\nTo start the ECU from power-up or reset, a fixed sequence of driver and manager\ninitialization is necessary to reach the required startup times and to set the FlexRay\nstack into working state. The sequence itself depends on many requirements, partly\ndependent on the FlexRay controller and the power supply concept⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00230] Initialize the FlexRay Transceiver Driver\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Fr_05137\n⌈The FlexRay Transceiver Driver shall provide an API to initialize the driver internally\nand set then all attached FlexRay Transceivers in their preselected operation modes.\n• The FlexRay Transceiver Driver must be initialized during the power-up/reset se-\nquence of the ECU.\n• Depending on the used drivers to control the transceivers (e.g. DIO, SPI), they\nmust be already available and working when the FlexRay Transceiver Driver is\ninitialized.\n• The wake-up reason has to be detected and stored during the execution of the\ndriver initialization, too.\n⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00270] ⌈The function FrTrcv_Init shall set all transceivers in the state\ndefined by the configuration parameter FRTRCV_INIT_STATE, i.e. in any state defined\nby [SWS_FrTrcv_00434].⌋\nNote that in the time span between power up and the call FrTrcv_Init the FlexRay\ntransceiver hardware may be in a different state. This depends on hardware and SPAL\ndriver configuration.\nThe initialization sequence after reset (e.g. power up) is a critical phase for the FlexRay\ntransceiver driver.\nNote: Before calling FrTrcv_Init the environment insures that all SPAL drivers used by\nthe FrTrcv module to access the transceiver hardware are initialized and usable.\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00437] ⌈In case of a fault during transceiver access, the initial-\nization process shall be restarted from the beginning.\nIt shall be retried un-\ntil the retry counter exceeds the number specified by FrTrcvRetryCountInInit.\nIf\nthe process doesn’t succeed, the function FrTrcv_Init shall raise a runtime error\nFRTRCV_E_FR_NO_CONTROL_TRCV (see also [SWS_FrTrcv_00237]).⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00390] ⌈If the configuration parameter FrTrcvErrorCheckInInit is\nset true,\nthe function FrTrcv_Init shall check state of ERRN to detect hard-\nware failure.\nIf an error is detected, FrTrcv_Init shall raise a production error\nFRTRCV_E_FR_ERRN_TRCV_<TrcvIdx>.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00438] ⌈The function FrTrcv_Init shall check whether there has been\na wake up due to transceiver activity if supported by hardware and report this to the\nEcuM via EcuM_SetWakeupEvent(event).⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00362] ⌈The driver has to notify ECU State Manager by invoking the\nEcuM_SetWakeupEvent service once only if a wakeup event is detected.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00363] ⌈The driver has to detect a pending wakeup event during the\ninitialization.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00065]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00358\n⌈The return type of init() functions implemented by AUTOSAR Basic Software Modules\nshall be void.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00366] ⌈The driver restart shall re-arm the trigger mechanism of the\n’wakeup detected’ call-back i. e. wake up events are enabled at driver initialization if\nconfigured accordingly and supported by hardware.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00367] ⌈The FlexRay Transceiver Driver driver shall support a wakeup\nISR if supported by hardware.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00414] Hardware Resetting Function on Bus Driver\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Fr_05214\n⌈The FlexRay Transceiver Driver shall provide a method that reinitializes BD’s function-\nality⌋\nHint: When trouble occurs in the hardware level, it is likely to fix the cause by resetting\nthe hardware. This function shall be executed when a configurable amount of errors\nare detected in by the FlexRay modules and have been reported to DEM.\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00455] ⌈If a transceiver is in active star mode and one or more\nbranches have been disabled, the FlexRay Transceiver Driver shall re-enable all\nbranches on initialization.⌋"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "8.3.2 FrTrcv_SetTransceiverMode\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00323] Definition of API function FrTrcv_SetTransceiverMode ⌈\nService Name\nFrTrcv_SetTransceiverMode\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType FrTrcv_SetTransceiverMode (\nuint8 FrTrcv_TrcvIdx,\nFrTrcv_TrcvModeType FrTrcv_TrcvMode\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x01\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nNon Reentrant\nFrTrcv_TrcvIdx\nThis zero based index identifies the transceiver within the context\nof the transceiver driver to which the API call has to be applied.\nParameters (in)\nFrTrcv_TrcvMode\nSelects the state the transceiver will transit to (transitions to\noptional states may fail)\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: will be returned if the transceiver state has been changed\nto the requested mode.\nE_NOT_OK: will be returned if the transceiver state change has\nfailed. The previous state has not been changed.\nDescription\nThis service sets the transceiver mode.\nAvailable via\nFrTrcv.h\n⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00252] Set FlexRay Transceiver Operation Mode\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Fr_05166\n⌈The FlexRay Transceiver Driver shall provide a software interface to set the operation\nmode of a specific FlexRay Transceiver device.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00392] ⌈Whenever FrTrcv_SetTransceiverMode changes the state to\nSTANDBY, it shall clear error history in transceiver as long as the hardware supports\nsuch a function.\nThis modification has the same effect as introducing a new API\nFrTrcv_ClearErrorHistory() and adding a call of the function in FrSm’s sequence.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00474] ⌈A mode request of the current mode is allowed and shall not\nlead to an error even if DET is enabled.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00064] Standard API return type\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00357\n⌈The Std_ReturnType shall normally be used with value E_OK or E_NOT_OK. If those\nreturn values are not sufficient user specific values can be defined by using the 6 least\nspecific bits.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00272] ⌈The function FrTrcv_SetTransceiverMode shall switch the in-\nternal state of the transceiver identified by FrTrcv_TrcvIdx to the state indicated by\nFrTrcv_TrcvMode.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00273]\n⌈The\nfunction\nFrTrcv_SetTransceiverMode\nshall\nreturn\nE_NOT_OK and doesn’t change the current state if a transition not defined in\nFrTrcv_TrcvModeType is requested.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00274] ⌈If an optional state is NOT supported by the transceiver and\nECU hardware, the function FrTrcv_SetTransceiverMode shall switch to an equivalent\nstate.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00440] ⌈If the FlexRay transceiver and ECU hardware does not support\na receive only state, FrTRCV_TRCVMODE_NORMAL shall be used.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00236] ⌈If the FlexRay transceiver and ECU hardware does not support\na sleep state, FrTRCV_TRCVMODE_STANDBY shall be used.\n(EcuM2486: The driver shall provide an explicit service to put the wakeup source to\nsleep. This service shall put the wakeup source into a energy saving and inert opera-\ntion mode and re-arm the wakeup notification mechanism.)⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00278]\n⌈In\ncase\nof\na\nfault\nduring\ntransceiver\nac-\ncess,\nthe\nfunction\nFrTrcv_SetTransceiverMode\nshall\nraise\nruntime\nerror\nFRTRCV_E_FR_NO_CONTROL_TRCV (see also [SWS_FrTrcv_00237]).⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00368] ⌈The API function calls to the FlexRay Transceiver Driver shall\nbe synchronuous.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00275]\n⌈If\ndevelopment\nerror\ndetection\nfor\nthe\nmodule\nFrTrcv\nis\nenabled:\nIf\nthe\nparameter\nFrTrcv_TrcvIdx\nis\nnot\nwithin\nthe\nallowed\nrange,\nthe\nfunction\nFrTrcv_SetTransceiverMode\nshall\nraise\ndevelopment\nerror\nFRTRCV_E_FR_INVALID_TRCVIDX.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00276] ⌈If the mode transition fails [SWS_FrTrcv_00452], the function\nFrTrcv_SetTransceiverMode shall raise the following runtime error:\n• FRTRCV_E_FR_TRCV_NOT_STANDBY:\nTransition to FRTRCV_TRCVMODE_STANDBY failed\n• FRTRCV_E_FR_TRCV_NOT_NORMAL:\nTransition to FRTRCV_TRCVMODE_NORMAL failed\n• FRTRCV_E_FR_TRCV_NOT_SLEEP:\nTransition to FRTRCV_TRCVMODE_SLEEP failed\n• FRTRCV_E_FR_TRCV_NOT_RECEIVEONLY:\nTransition to FRTRCV_TRCVMODE_RECEIVEONLY failed\n⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00452] ⌈A mode transition fails, if the mode returned by the API service\nFrTrcv_GetTransceiverMode() would mismatch the mode requested by the API service\nFrTrcv_SetTransceiverMode().⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00277]\n⌈If\ndevelopment\nerror\ndetection\nfor\nthe\nmodule\nFrTrcv is enabled:\nif the transceiver has not been initialized,\nthe function\nFrTrcv_SetTransceiverMode shall raise development error FRTRCV_E_UNINIT.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00415] Hardware Checking Function on Bus Driver\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Fr_05213\n⌈The FlexRay Transceiver Driver’s initialization function shall check error status in BD\nto ensure the hardware is working properly.\nThis functionality ensures that the hardware is working as expected.\nImprovement of hardware reliability.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00454] ⌈If a transceiver is in active star mode and one or more\nbranches are disabled, the FlexRay Transceiver Driver shall avoid side effects of the\nAPI service FrTrcv_SetTransceiverMode() which re-enable any branches.⌋"

      "verbatim_text": "8.3.3 FrTrcv_GetTransceiverMode\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00324] Definition of API function FrTrcv_GetTransceiverMode ⌈\nService Name\nFrTrcv_GetTransceiverMode\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType FrTrcv_GetTransceiverMode (\nuint8 FrTrcv_TrcvIdx,\nFrTrcv_TrcvModeType* FrTrcv_TrcvModePtr\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x05\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant\nParameters (in)\nFrTrcv_TrcvIdx\nThis zero based index identifies the transceiver within the context\nof the transceiver driver to which the API call has to be applied.\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nFrTrcv_TrcvModePtr\nPointer to structure of current transceiver state; the FlexRay\ntransceiver driver will write the transceiver state information there.\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: will be returned if the transceiver state has been provided\nE_NOT_OK: will be returned if the parameter is out of range.\nOutput parameters remain unchanged.\nDescription\nThis function returns the actual state of the transceiver.\nAvailable via\nFrTrcv.h\n⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00253]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Fr_05167\n⌈The function FrTrcv_GetTransceiverMode shall return the state of the transceiver iden-\ntified by FrTrcv_TrcvIdx.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00281]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Fr_05151\n⌈In case of a fault during transceiver access, the function FrTrcv_GetTransceiverMode\nshall raise the runtime error FRTRCV_E_FR_NO_CONTROL_TRCV (see also\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00237]).⌋\nSee FrTrcv_Init ([SWS_FrTrcv_00270]) for the provided state after the FlexRay\ntransceiver driver initialization until the first operation mode change request.\nThe number of supported FlexRay transceivers and their type is statically set in the\nconfiguration phase.\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00279]\n⌈If\ndevelopment\nerror\ndetection\nfor\nthe\nmodule\nFrTrcv\nis\nenabled:\nif\nthe\nparameter\nFrTrcv_TrcvIdx\nis\nout\nof\nrange,\nthe\nfunction\nFrTrcv_GetTransceiverMode\nshall\nraise\nthe\ndevelopment\nerror\nFRTRCV_E_FR_INVALID_TRCVIDX.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00280]\n⌈If\ndevelopment\nerror\ndetection\nfor\nthe\nmodule\nFrTrcv is enabled:\nif the transceiver has not been initialized,\nthe function\nFrTrcv_GetTransceiverMode shall raise the development error FRTRCV_E_UNINIT.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00397] ⌈When the caller provides a NULL pointer as a parameter value\nto the API FrTrcv_GetTransceiverMode, the return value shall be E_NOT_OK and the\ndevelopment error FRTRCV_E_PARAM_POINTER shall be reported to DET if devel-\nopment error detection is enabled.⌋"

      "verbatim_text": "8.3.4 FrTrcv_GetTransceiverWUReason\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00325] Definition of API function FrTrcv_GetTransceiverWURea-\nson ⌈\nService Name\nFrTrcv_GetTransceiverWUReason\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType FrTrcv_GetTransceiverWUReason (\nuint8 FrTrcv_TrcvIdx,\nFrTrcv_TrcvWUReasonType* FrTrcv_TrcvWUReasonPtr\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x06\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant\nParameters (in)\nFrTrcv_TrcvIdx\nThis zero based index identifies the transceiver within the context\nof the transceiver driver to which the API call has to be applied.\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nFrTrcv_TrcvWUReasonPtr\nPointer to structure of least recent wakeup source, the FlexRay\ntransceiver driver will write the transceiver wakeup reason\ninformation.\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: will be returned if the transceiver wake up source has been\nprovided\nE_NOT_OK: will be returned if the transceiver wakeup reason is\nnot defined in FrTrcv_TrcvWUReasonType. Output parameters\nremain unchanged.\nDescription\nThis function returns the wakeup reason.\nAvailable via\nFrTrcv.h\n⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00232]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Fr_05144\n⌈The function FrTrcv_GetTransceiverWUReason shall return the reason for the wake\nup that the FlexRay transceiver identified by FrTrcv_TrcvIdx has detected if supported\nby hardware.\nThe ability to detect and differentiate the possible wake up reasons depends strongly\non the FlexRay transceiver hardware.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00284]\n⌈In\ncase\nof\na\nfault\nduring\ntransceiver\naccess,\nthe\nfunction\nFrTrcv_GetTransceiverWUReason\nshall\nraise\nruntime\nerror\nFRTRCV_E_FR_NO_CONTROL_TRCV (see also [SWS_FrTrcv_00237]).⌋\nPlease be aware, that if more than one bus is available, each bus may report a different\nwake up reason. E.g. if an ECU has FlexRay, a wake up by FlexRay may occur and\nthe incoming data may cause an internal wake up for another FlexRay bus.\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00453] ⌈The FlexRay Transceiver Driver shall report the wake up rea-\nson in the order defined by [SWS_FrTrcv_00074].Thus, FRTRCV_WU_BY_BUS is re-\nported first in case of multiple concurrent events.⌋\nThe FlexRay bus transceiver driver has a \"per bus\" view and does not vote the more\nimportant reason or sequence internally. The same may be true if e.g. one transceiver\ncontrols the power supply and the other is just powered or un-powered. Then one\nmay be able to return \"FRTRCV_WU_POWER_ON\" whereas the other may state e.g.\n\"FRTRCV_WU_RESET\".\nIt is up to the EcuM and the ComM, to decide what shall happen with that wake up\ninformation.\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00282]\n⌈If\ndevelopment\nerror\ndetection\nof\nthe\nmodule\nFrTrcv\nis\nenabled:\nif\nthe\nparameter\nFrTrcv_TrcvIdx\nis\nout\nof\nrange,\nthe\nfunc-\ntion\nFrTrcv_GetTransceiverWUReason\nshall\nraise\nthe\ndevelopment\nerror\nFRTRCV_E_FR_INVALID_TRCVIDX.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00283]\n⌈If\ndevelopment\nerror\ndetection\nof\nthe\nmodule\nFrTrcv\nis\nenabled:\nif\nthe\ntransceiver\nhas\nnot\nbeen\ninitialized,\nthe\nfunc-\ntion\nFrTrcv_GetTransceiverWUReason\nshall\nraise\nthe\ndevelopment\nerror\nFRTRCV_E_UNINIT.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00398] ⌈When the caller provides a NULL pointer as a param-\neter value to the API FrTrcv_GetTransceiverWUReason, the development error\nFRTRCV_E_PARAM_POINTER shall be reported to DET if development error detec-\ntion is enabled.⌋"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "8.3.5 FrTrcv_GetVersionInfo\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00326] Definition of API function FrTrcv_GetVersionInfo ⌈\nService Name\nFrTrcv_GetVersionInfo\nSyntax\nvoid FrTrcv_GetVersionInfo (\nStd_VersionInfoType* versioninfo\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x07\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant\nParameters (in)\nNone\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nversioninfo\nPointer to structure with version information.\nReturn value\nNone\nDescription\nThis service returns the version information of this module.\nAvailable via\nFrTrcv.h\n⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00001] Version identification\nUpstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00003\n⌈The FlexRay transceiver driver shall support a version information API.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00285] ⌈The function FrTrcv_GetVersionInfo shall return the version in-\nformation of the FrTrcv module, NOT the version of the FlexRay transceiver hardware.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00396] ⌈When a NULL pointer is passed as a parameter value of\nFrTrcv_GetVersionInfo, the development error FRTRCV_E_PARAM_POINTER shall\nbe reported to DETshall be reported to DET if development error detection is enabled.⌋"

      "verbatim_text": "8.3.6 FrTrcv_ClearTransceiverWakeup\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00329] Definition of API function FrTrcv_ClearTransceiverWakeup\n⌈\nService Name\nFrTrcv_ClearTransceiverWakeup\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType FrTrcv_ClearTransceiverWakeup (\nuint8 FrTrcv_TrcvIdx\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x0c\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nNon Reentrant\nParameters (in)\nFrTrcv_TrcvIdx\nThis zero based index identifies the transceiver within the context\nof the transceiver driver to which the API call has to be applied.\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: will be returned if the transceiver wake up source has been\ncleared\nE_NOT_OK: will be returned if the parameter FrTrcv_TrcvIdx is out\nof range. Wake up state remains unchanged.\nDescription\nThis function clears a pending wake up event.\nAvailable via\nFrTrcv.h\n⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00247]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Fr_05161\n⌈The function FrTrcv_ClearTransceiverWakeup shall clear a pending wake up event on\nthe transceiver identified by FrTrcv_TrcvIdx.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00371] ⌈The API shall clear all pending wake up events under control\nof the higher layer. It may even be used if the wake up notification is disabled.⌋\nIn order to keep the transceiver driver simple, this API refers to all kinds of wake up.\nFurther differentiation of wakeup sources requires knowledge available only to higher\nsoftware layers and is out of scope of the transceiver driver.\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00306]\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Fr_05151\n⌈In\ncase\nof\na\nfault\nduring\ntransceiver\naccess,\nthe\nfunc-\ntion\nFrTrcv_ClearTransceiverWakeup\nshall\nraise\nthe\nruntime\nerror\nFRTRCV_E_FR_NO_CONTROL_TRCV (see also [SWS_FrTrcv_00237]).⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00304] ⌈If development error detection is enabled for the mod-\nule\nFrTrcv:\nif\nthe\nparameter\nFrTrcv_TrcvIdx\nis\nout\nof\nrange,\nthe\nfunc-\ntion\nFrTrcv_ClearTransceiverWakeup\nshall\nraise\nthe\ndevelopment\nerror\ncode\nFRTRCV_E_FR_INVALID_TRCVIDX.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00305]\n⌈If\ndevelopment\nerror\ndetection\nis\nenabled\nfor\nthe\nmodule\nFrTrcv:\nif\nthe\ntransceiver\nhas\nnot\nbeen\ninitialized,\nthe\nfunction\nFrTrcv_ClearTransceiverWakeup\nshall\nraise\nthe\ndevelopment\nerror\ncode\nFRTRCV_E_UNINIT.⌋"

    {
      "id": "SNIP_CLASSIC_FRTRCV_SECTION_8_3_7_FrTrcv_CheckWakeupByTransceiver",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "SWS_FlexRayTransceiverDriver",
      "source_page": 46,
      "category": null,
      "relevance_score": 0.85,
      "disposition": "UNVERIFIED",
      "evidence_status": "unverified_hypothesis",
      "guideline": "⚠️ Zwingend als UNVERIFIED AI HYPOTHESIS kennzeichnen mit Warnbox und Inline-Curation-Link",
      "verbatim_text": "8.3.7 FrTrcv_CheckWakeupByTransceiver\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00331]\nDefinition of callback function FrTrcv_CheckWakeupBy\nTransceiver ⌈\nService Name\nFrTrcv_CheckWakeupByTransceiver\nSyntax\nvoid FrTrcv_CheckWakeupByTransceiver (\nuint8 FrTrcv_TrcvIdx\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x0e\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nReentrant\nParameters (in)\nFrTrcv_TrcvIdx\nThis zero based index identifies the transceiver within the context\nof the transceiver driver to which the API call has to be applied\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nNone\nDescription\n--\nAvailable via\nFrTrcv.h\n⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00364] ⌈The driver shall notify ECU State Manager of wakeup events if\ntriggered by the API call FrTrcv_CheckWakeupByTransceiver.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00233] Notification for Wake-up by Bus\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Fr_05147\n⌈The FlexRay Transceiver Driver shall support a notification to inform higher layers\nabout the wake-up by bus. It must be possible to support more than one bus within the\nECU with this notification.\nThe FlexRay Transceiver Driver shall call this notification when the transceiver detects\na wake-up by bus.\nThe FlexRay Transceiver Driver is notified by a notification from the underlying SPI or\nDIO driver in that case. The notification is executed in the context of the caller (may\nbe interrupt context!). Because the delay from wake-up detection until the start of the\nnecessary actions has a large influence on the startup time of an ECU, this event shall\nbe processed internally and transferred immediately via this notification to the next\nlayer.\nThe call context and the reaction time depend on the call context of the lower layer DIO\nor SPI. In case of interrupt it is very fast but data consistency issues must be covered\nin all layers. In case of polling data consistency issues are reduced but reaction time\nmay be too slow.\nRationale: Support wake-up by FlexRay Transceiver devices.\nUse Case: The FlexRay Transceiver detects a wake-up condition on the bus and shows\nthis to the µC via e.g. a port pin.\nFurther handling depends on current ECU state. Assuming the ECU is halted, the\nchange on the port may terminate the \"HALT\" statement and let the processor continue\nits work. The assigned port interrupt will be executed and this handler is called. Now,\nthe FlexRay Transceiver Driver will store the wake-up reason and give the call via this\nnotification to e.g. the NM to let the NM decide how to handle the event.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00262] ⌈EcuM2483: The driver has to notify ECU State Manager by\ninvoking the EcuM_SetWakeupEvent service once when a wakeup event is detected.\nThe same service should also be invoked during initialization of the driver if a pending\nwakeup event is detected during the initialization. Preferably, the invocation is done\nfrom a callout or function stub of the caller, to decouple driver modules and ECU State\nManager.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00311]\n⌈The\nfunction\nFrTrcv_CheckWakeupByTransceiver()\nshall\ncall\nthe\nAPI\nservice\nEcuM_SetWakeupEvent\nwith\nthe\nparameter\nvalue\nECUM_WKSOURCE_FRTRCV_FR of EcuM_WakeupSourceType only in case a\nvalid wakeup originated from the transceiver identified by FrTrcv_TrcvIdx. Thus, shared\ninterrupts are easily de-multiplexed: Drivers just return doing nothing if they did not\ntrigger the interrupt.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00374] ⌈The function FrTrcv_CheckWakeupByTransceiver() shall clear\na pending wake up event on the transceiver identified by FrTrcv_TrcvIdx after the last\ncall of EcuM (EcuM_SetWakeupEvent). Wake up by bus is always asynchronous to\nthe transition to sleep and standby. In worst case wake up occurs during transition to\nsleep.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00375] ⌈The FlexRay Transceiver Driver shall check for wake up events\nimmediately after the API call FrTrcv_SetTransceiverMode if supported by hardware.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00378] ⌈If no wake up by bus is used this function need not be\npresent in compiled code. See configuration parameters FrTrcvWakeupByBusUsed\n[ECUC_FrTrcv_00350] for more details.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00379] ⌈Calling FrTrcv_CheckWakeupByTransceiver in an interrupt\ncontext shall be supported.\nHint: This has to be documented according to [SRS_\nBSW_00333]).\nHint: While the ECU is in SLEEP, the main function () is not scheduled yet, but the\nwake up reason has to be identified by the FlexRay Transceiver Driver in the context of\nthe wake up interrupt.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00380] ⌈Calling FrTrcv_CheckWakeupByTransceiver by a polling pro-\ncess in sleep mode shall be supported.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00312]\n⌈If\ndevelopment\nerror\ndetection\nof\nmodule\nFrTrcv\nis\nenabled:\nif\nthe\nparameter\nFrTrcv_TrcvIdx\nis\nout\nof\nrange,\nthe\nfunc-\ntion\nFrTrcv_CheckWakeupByTransceiver\nshall\nraise\ndevelopment\nerror\nFRTRCV_E_FR_INVALID_TRCVIDX.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00313] ⌈If development error detection of module FrTrcv is enabled: if\nthe FrTrcv module is not initialized, the function FrTrcv_CheckWakeupByTransceiver\nshall raise development error FRTRCV_E_UNINIT.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00229] Configuration \"Notification for Wake-up by Bus\"\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Fr_05136\n⌈The FlexRay Transceiver Driver shall support the compile time configuration of one\nnotification to a higher layer for change notification for \"wake-up by bus\" events.\nOne wake-up by bus event notification shall be supported to one higher layer.\nIf a transceiver device does not support \"wake-up by bus\", this notification is never\ncalled for this bus.\nEfficient coupling between FlexRay Transceiver Driver and higher layer.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00234] Support for Wake-up During Sleep Transition\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Fr_05148\n⌈The FlexRay Transceiver Driver shall support situations where a wake-up by bus oc-\ncurs at the same moment the transition to standby/sleep is executed by the driver.\nWake-up by bus is always asynchronous to the internal transition to sleep.\nIn worst case, the wake-up occurs during the transition to sleep. This situation must\nbe covered by the design and explicitly tested for each ECU. The driver shall create a\nwake-up notification by bus immediately after the API to enter the standby/sleep mode\nhas finished.\nThe calling/controlling component (NM or ECU state manager) must be capable to\nhandle the wake-up immediately after requesting the standby/sleep.\nSafe wake-up and sleep handling.\nAll busses with a wake-up by bus are affected.⌋"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "8.3.8 FrTrcv_GetTransceiverError\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00419] Definition of API function FrTrcv_GetTransceiverError ⌈\nService Name\nFrTrcv_GetTransceiverError\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType FrTrcv_GetTransceiverError (\nuint8 FrTrcv_TrcvIdx,\nuint8 FrTrcv_BranchIdx,\nuint32* FrTrcv_BusErrorState\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x08\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nNon Reentrant\nFrTrcv_TrcvIdx\nThis zero based index identifies the transceiver within the context\nof the transceiver driver to which the API call has to be applied.\nParameters (in)\nFrTrcv_BranchIdx\nThis zero based index identifies the branch of the (active star)\ntransceiver to which the API call has to be applied.\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nFrTrcv_BusErrorState\nPointer to structure of detailed transceiver error state;\n• Parameter is reference to variable:\nThe transceiver driver will write the current transceiver error state\ninformation according to FrTrcv420 there, if the transceiver\nsupports this information.\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: will be returned if the transceiver error state has been\nprovided\nE_NOT_OK: will be returned if the parameter FrTrcv_TrcvIdx or Fr\nTrcv_BranchIdx is out of range or the transceiver error state is not\navailable. Output parameters remain unchanged.\nDescription\nAll mandatory errors defined by the FlexRay EPL [5] which are supported by the FlexRay\ntransceiver hardware can be accessed via this API:In addition to errors on the physical layer\nand local to the ECU hardware, a global error flag is provided.\nAvailable via\nFrTrcv.h\n⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00412] Detect Error Information in Bus Driver\nUpstream requirements: SRS_Fr_05212\n⌈The FlexRay Transceiver Driver shall provide an API that detects errors in the bus\ndriver and notifies the application level.\nThe FlexRay modules should provide information that only the modules can detect.⌋\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00420] FlexRay Transceiver Driver mandatory errors ⌈\nAvailability\nTopology\nDescription\nBit\nMandatory\nGlobal error\nAny of the mandatory errors defined in this\ntable, please see [SWS_FrTrcv_00457],\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00458]\n0\nMandatory\non the bus (i. e. external to the ECU):\nShort circuit between bus lines according\nto [1, FlexRay EPL]"
    },

      "verbatim_text": "8.3.9 FrTrcv_DisableTransceiverBranch\nThe FlexRay Transceiver Driver shall disable the faulty branches of active stars\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00442]\nDefinition of API function FrTrcv_DisableTransceiver\nBranch ⌈\nService Name\nFrTrcv_DisableTransceiverBranch\nSyntax\nStd_ReturnType FrTrcv_DisableTransceiverBranch (\nuint8 FrTrcv_TrcvIdx,\nuint8 FrTrcv_BranchIdx\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x0f\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nNon Reentrant\nFrTrcv_TrcvIdx\nThis zero based index identifies the transceiver within the context\nof the transceiver driver to which the API call has to be applied.\nParameters (in)\nFrTrcv_BranchIdx\nThis zero based index identifies the branch of the (active star)\ntransceiver to which the API call has to be applied.\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nStd_ReturnType\nE_OK: will be returned if the transceiver branch has been disabled\nE_NOT_OK: will be returned if the parameter FrTrcv_TrcvIdx or Fr\nTrcv_BranchIdx is out of range.       "verbatim_text": "8.5.1 FrTrcv_MainFunction\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00330] Definition of API function FrTrcv_MainFunction ⌈\nService Name\nFrTrcv_MainFunction\nSyntax\nvoid FrTrcv_MainFunction (\nvoid\n)\nService ID [hex]\n0x0d\nSync/Async\nSynchronous\nReentrancy\nNon Reentrant\nParameters (in)\nNone\nParameters (inout)\nNone\nParameters (out)\nNone\nReturn value\nNone\nDescription\n–\nAvailable via\nSchM_FrTrcv.h\n⌋()\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00020] ⌈Compatibility and documentation of scheduling strategy: The\nFlexRay bus transceiver driver may have cyclic jobs like polling for wake up events (if\nconfigured). The period of the main function is defined by configuration.⌋(SRS_BSW_-\n00172)\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00072] ⌈Main processing function naming convention: The main func-\ntion of the FlexRay transceiver driver shall be named FrTrcv_MainFunction.⌋(SRS_-\nBSW_00373)\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00126] ⌈Execution order dependencies of main processing functions:\nThe main processing function of the FlexRay transceiver driver shall be independent of\nthe FlexRay bus schedule i. e. it may be scheduled either synchronous to the FlexRay\nbus schedule as well as asynchronous to the FlexRay bus schedule.⌋(SRS_BSW_-\n00428)\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00340] ⌈The function FrTrcv_MainFunction shall scan all busses in\nSTANDBY and SLEEP for wake up events and store them internally.⌋()\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00122] ⌈The function FrTrcv_MainFunction shall be implemented in\nsuch a way that it can run inside a basic task (scheduled by the AUTOSAR RTE).⌋\n(SRS_BSW_00424)\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00372]\n⌈The\nBasic\nSoftware\nScheduler\nshall\nexe-\ncute\nFrTrcv_MainFunction\nwith\na\nperiod\nconfigured\nby\nthe\nparameter\nFRTRCV_MAIN_FUNCTION_CYCLE_TIME. See [ECUC_FrTrcv_00343] for more\ndetails.⌋()\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00373] ⌈If no cycle time is configured for the FrTrcv_MainFunction\n(multiplicity of FrTrcvMainFunctionCycleTime is 0) this function is not executed by\nthe Basic Software Scheduler and need not be present in compiled code.\nSee\n[ECUC_FrTrcv_00343] for more details.⌋()\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00123] Trigger conditions for schedulable objects ⌈The BSW mod-\nule description template shall provide means to model the following trigger conditions\nof schedulable objects:\n• Cyclic timings (fixed and selectable during runtime)\n• Sporadic events\n⌋(SRS_BSW_00425)\n[SWS_FrTrcv_00436]\n⌈The\nFrTrcv_MainFunction\nshall\ncall\nFrTrcv_GetTransceiverError () periodically to detect error information in BD if\nFrTrcvErrorCheckDuringCommunication is enabled.⌋(SRS_Fr_05203)\nNote: The FlexRay modules should provide information that only the modules can\ndetect.\nApplications could take actions to recover the failure cause like resetting the modules\nwhen they receive this error information."

Std_ReturnType FrTp_TriggerTransmit (PduIdType TxPduId, PduInfoType* PduInfoPtr);

            
Within this API , the upper layer module (called module) shall check whether the available data fits into the buffer size reported by Pdu Info Ptr - >Sdu Length. If it fits, it shall copy its data into the buffer provided by Pdu Info Ptr - >Sdu Data Ptr and update the length of the actual copied data in Pdu Info Ptr - >Sdu Length. If not, it returns E_ NOT_ OK without changing Pdu Info Ptr.

Zweck: Beleg aus SWS_FlexRayDriver (5 Dependencies to other modules).

            
5 Dependencies to other modules
This chapter lists the modules interacting with the Fr module.
Modules that use Fr module:
• The FrIf is the only user of the Fr module (except initialization by EcuM). It uses
the Fr module(s) to access possibly different FlexRay Communication Controllers
in a uniform and abstract way.
• The EcuM initializes the Fr module by calling Fr_Init.
Modules used by the Fr module:
• [SWS_Fr_00453] ⌈The Fr module shall use the BSW Scheduler mechanisms for
data consistency when required.⌋
Other Module dependencies:
• [SWS_Fr_00454] ⌈On certain systems the CC might share resources with other
components (e.g., the MCU), and might depend on their configurations. If those
resources are within the scope of the other modules (e.g., PLL configuration,
memory mapping), then the Fr module doesn’t configure those components but
requires that their initialization precede the Fr module’s initialization.⌋

Zweck: Beleg aus SWS_FlexRayDriver (7.3 Indexing Scheme).

            
7.3 Indexing Scheme
Users of the Fr identify Fr resources by using an indexing scheme as depicted in
Figure 7.1.
Figure 7.1: FlexRay Driver indexing scheme
The following Fr resources are available:
[SWS_Fr_00075]
Upstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00413
⌈CCs are identified via controller indices (Fr_CtrlIdx).⌋
[SWS_Fr_00467]
Upstream requirements: SRS_Fr_05065
⌈Each driver’s CCs are identified by controller indices 0 to (n-1) where n is the number
of CCs controlled by the particular Fr.⌋
[SWS_Fr_00344] ⌈For each FlexRay CC the connected channels are identified by
channel indices (Fr_ChnlIdx).⌋
[SWS_Fr_00468] ⌈A dedicated type that holds the enumerations FR_CHANNEL_A,
FR_CHANNEL_B or FR_CHANNEL_AB represents the channel index.⌋
[SWS_Fr_00469] ⌈Channel indices are only valid within a tuple Fr_ChnlIdx>.⌋
[SWS_Fr_00005]
Upstream requirements: SRS_Fr_05003, SRS_Fr_05024
⌈Each FlexRay frame processed by Fr API functions is identified by an LPdu index (
Fr_LPduIdx).⌋
[SWS_Fr_00470] ⌈Each LPdu carries the LSdu. Each controller’s LPdus are identified
by LPdu indices from 0 to (n-1) where n is the number of LPdus processed by the
corresponding CC.⌋
[SWS_Fr_00471] ⌈LPdu indices are only valid within a tuple Fr_LPduIdx>.⌋
[SWS_Fr_00472] ⌈An Fr_LPduIdx uniquely identifies the following parameters of a
FlexRay frame as a key: {Slot ID, Channel, cycle repetition, base cycle, transmit/re-
ceive}.⌋
[SWS_Fr_00345] ⌈Each FlexRay CC contains absolute timers.
Absolute FlexRay
timers are identified via absolute timer indices (Fr_AbsTimerIdx).⌋
[SWS_Fr_00473] ⌈Each CC’s absolute timers are identified by absolute timer indices
from 0 to (n-1), where n is the number of absolute timers controlled by the particular
CC.⌋
[SWS_Fr_00474] ⌈Absolute timer indices are only valid within a tuple Fr_AbsTimerIdx>.⌋
The FlexRay Driver numbering scheme (Figure 7.1) assigns indices to these items on
a per-driver basis. Note that only the FlexRay CCs handled by one specific Fr module
(i.e., the FlexRay CCs of type A in the example given) are being assigned indices within
the context of this Fr module. All other CCs (e.g., the FlexRay CC of type B) are not
handled by this Fr module and thus no indices have been assigned to these FlexRay
CCs within the context of this Fr module.

Table 7.8: Layout of FlexRay FrameID
[SWS_Mirror_00104]
Upstream requirements: SRS_Mirror_00008
⌈The width of the FrameIDFlexRay field shall be 3 bytes.⌋
[SWS_Mirror_00105]
Upstream requirements: SRS_Mirror_00008
⌈Bits 7 – 6 of Byte 0 of the FrameIDFlexRay shall contain the channel assignment
of the reported FlexRay frame. Bit 7 shall be set to 1 if the reported FlexRay frame is
available on channel B of the FlexRay controller, otherwise it shall be set to 0. Bit 6
shall be set to 1 if the reported FlexRay frame is available on channel A of the FlexRay
controller, otherwise it shall be set to 0. A reported FlexRay frame is either assigned
exclusively to channel A or B or to both channels.⌋
This layout of the channel assignment corresponds to the Fr_ChannelType reported
by Mirror_ReportFlexRayFrame.
[SWS_Mirror_00106]
Upstream requirements: SRS_Mirror_00008
⌈Bits 5 – 4 of Byte 0 of the FrameIDFlexRay are currently reserved. They shall
always be set 0.⌋
[SWS_Mirror_00159]
Upstream requirements: SRS_Mirror_00008
⌈Bit 3 of Byte 0 of the FrameIDFlexRay shall contain a flag indicating whether the
reported slot ID and cycle are valid (flag is 1) or unused (flag is 0). It shall only be set
to 0 when an aggregated error of the FlexRay channels is reported independently of a
source frame or transmission conflict. Otherwise it shall always be set to 1.⌋
[SWS_Mirror_00107]
Upstream requirements: SRS_Mirror_00008
⌈Bits 2 – 0 of Byte 0 and Byte 1 of the FrameIDFlexRay shall contain the slot ID of
the reported FlexRay frame in network byte order (MSB first).⌋
[SWS_Mirror_00108]
Upstream requirements: SRS_Mirror_00008
⌈Byte 2 of the FrameIDFlexRay shall contain the cycle in which the reported FlexRay
frame was sent or received.⌋
Please note: For received frames and for frames sent in the static segment, the cycle
is always reliable. For frames sent in the dynamic segment, the actual cycle cannot be
known in advance, because the frame might not be transmitted in the planned cycle.

Zweck: Beleg aus SWS_FlexRayDriver (7.4 POC state machine control).

            
7.4 POC state machine control
[SWS_Fr_00477] ⌈Since a FlexRay CC is condition-based, it internally maintains a
state machine, the Protocol Operation Control (POC) state machine. The state transi-
tions are driven both by hardware related events as well as by commands passed by
the host at the CHI (see [1] for details).⌋
[SWS_Fr_00478] ⌈The CHI commands driving the POC state machine are incorpo-
rated into several Fr module API functions. API functions affecting the POC state of a
FlexRay CC are:
• Fr_StartCommunication()
• Fr_HaltCommunication()
• Fr_AbortCommunication()
• Fr_SendWUP()
• Fr_ControllerInit()
⌋
[SWS_Fr_00438] ⌈All API functions other than those listed above shall not change the
POC state of the FlexRay CC. Figure 3 shows the POC states of the FlexRay CC and
the transitions applicable to the Fr module API functions. Note that
• certain transitions (marked with *)) are performed by the invocation of a single
API function call (Fr_ControllerInit()).
• certain transitions might be implicitly performed by the FlexRay CC without exter-
nal command invocation (dotted arrow)
• certain transitions specified cannot be performed by the current Fr module API
(not drawn in Figure 3 - compare to [5]).
⌋
Figure 7.2: FlexRay Driver POC State Machine Control

Zweck: Beleg aus SWS_FlexRayDriver (7.5 FIFO support and message ID filtering).

            
7.5 FIFO support and message ID filtering
To efficiently support reception in certain use-cases, FlexRay controllers might support
receive-FIFOs. The receive-FIFOs accept FlexRay frames based on a set of configured
filter criterias which match FlexRay specific properties such as frameID, cycle, channel,
as well as protocol add-ons like the message ID, in hardware.
[SWS_Fr_00593] ⌈The hardware receive-FIFO shall be used if the FIFO filter-criterias
as configured can be applied to the hardware FIFO.⌋(SRS_Fr_05005, SRS_Fr_05006)
[SWS_Fr_00594] ⌈All LPdus (as configured within FrIf) matching a receive-FIFO’s
filter-criteria shall be assigned to the respective receive-FIFO.⌋(SRS_Fr_05005)
[SWS_Fr_00595] ⌈No specific buffers shall be assigned to LPdus that are assigned to
a receive-FIFO.⌋(SRS_Fr_05005)
[SWS_Fr_00596] ⌈If Fr_ReceiveRxLPdu() is called for an LPdu assigned to the re-
ceive FIFO, the service Fr_ReceiveRxPdu() consumes the first valid frame out of the
respective FIFO and returns it as received frame. There is no receive-FIFO specific
API, thus keeping the upper layers unaffected.⌋(SRS_Fr_05005)
Hint: This restricted implementation of the receive-FIFO covers a very typical use-case
(FrTp):
• All received (L)Pdus assigned to the FIFO shall be processed by a single upper
layer module.
• The upper layer does not care about the specific assignment of (L)Pdus to
FlexRay FrameTriggerings.
[SWS_Fr_00597] ⌈LPdus received via the FIFO shall be returned in the same order
as they were received on the FlexRay network.⌋(SRS_Fr_05005)

7.6.5.2 ProvideTxConfirmation
This Communication Operation provides a Tx confirmation and optionally checks the
occurrence of a Tx conflict.
[SWS_FrIf_05064] ⌈If the related CC is in FrIf_State FRIF_STATE_ONLINE for a Com-
munication Operation TX_CONFIRMATION, then the Job List Execution Function shall
execute this Communication Operation. Otherwise, the Job List Execution Function
shall ignore this Communication Operation.⌋
[SWS_FrIf_05288] ⌈"For a Communication Operation TX_CONFIRMATION the Job
List Execution Function shall perform the following steps:
1. Call the FlexRay Driver’s API function Fr_CheckTxLPduStatus():
• Fr_CtrlIdx is derived according to the indexing scheme described in chapter
of indexing
• Fr_LPduIdx is set to the configured L-PDU buffer index [Configuration Pa-
rameter FrIfLPduIdx, see FrIf06058] associated with the Communication Op-
eration.
• Fr_SlotAssignmentPtr is set to a temporary slot assignment buffer if Bus
Mirroring is enabled globally (see FrIfBusMirroringSupport), otherwise to the
NULL_PTR.
2. If the transmission was performed (output parameter *Fr_TxLPduStatusPtr is set
to FR_TRANSMITTED) then iterate over all PDUs contained in the FrIfFrame
Structure (see FrIf05370) of the associated frame triggering. If TxConfCounter
for a PDU is 0 proceed with the next PDU, otherwise
• If FrIfConfirm == true, call the upper layer’s function LSduR_FrIfTxConfirma-
tion(E_OK) with the asociated PDUId (defined by the upper layer).
• If FrIfConfirm == true , decrement TxConfCounter.
3. If the transmission was performed but a TxConflict occurred (output parameter
*Fr_TxLPduStatusPtr is set to FR_TRANSMITTED_CONFLICT) then iterate over
all PDUs contained in the FrIfFrameStructure (see FrIf05370) of the associated
frame triggering. If TxConfCounter for a PDU is 0 proceed with the next PDU,
otherwise
• If FrIfConfirm == true, call the upper layer’s function NOT_OK)> with the asociated PDUId (defined by the upper layer).
• If FrIfConfirm == true , decrement TxConfCounter.
4. If Bus Mirroring is enabled globally (see FrIfBusMirroringSupport) and has been
activated with a call to FrIf_EnableBusMirroring() for the Fr_CtrlIdx and the API
Fr_CheckTxLpduStatus() returns "FR_TRANSMITTED_CONFLICT", call Mirror_
ReportFlexRayFrame() with "controllerId" set to Fr_CtrlIdx, "slotId", "cycle", and
"channel" taken from Fr_SlotAssignmentPtr, "frame" set to the NULL_PTR, and
"txConflict" set to true.
If the API Fr_CheckTxLpduStatus() returns "FR_TRANSMITTED_CONFLICT" and the
 is configured via FrIfTxConflictNotificationName (ECUC_
FrIf_06122), call this function for the same LPduIdx.⌋

Zweck: Beleg aus SWS_FlexRayInterface (7.6.5.6 PREP ARE_LPDU).

            
7.6.5.6 PREPARE_LPDU
The Communication Operation PREPARE_LPDU enables hardware optimization
purposes (hardware buffer re-configuration)
[SWS_FrIf_05294] ⌈The Communication Operation PREPARE_LPDU performs the
following steps:
1. Call the FlexRay Driver’s API function Fr_PrepareLPdu():
• Fr_CtrlIdx is derived according to the indexing scheme described in chapter
of indexing.
• Fr_LPduIdx is set to the configured L-PDU index [Configuration Parameter
FrIfLPduIdx, see FrIf06058] associated with the Communication Operation.
⌋
[SWS_FrIf_05061]
Upstream requirements: SRS_Fr_05042
⌈The Communication Operation PREPARE_LPDU enables hardware optimization pur-
poses. Its purpose is to enable certain FlexRay CC hardware resources (e.g. a CC’s
message buffer) to be prepared (configured) for the transmission/reception of a certain
L-PDU.
This Communication Operation enables the FlexRay Driver to optimize the usage of
hardware resources if available at appropriate point of times. However, it is the respon-
sibility of the FlexRay Driver to decide and validate ressource allocation optimizations
based on the PREPARE_LPDU Communication Operations. Practically the usage of
this Communication Operation will introduce some runtime-overhead even if the Flex
Ray Driver does not use the opportunity for reconfiguration.⌋

Zweck: Beleg aus SWS_FlexRayDriver (7.6 Configuration description).

            
7.6 Configuration description
[SWS_Fr_00080]
Upstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00003, SRS_BSW_00334, SRS_BSW_00374, SRS_BSW_
00379
⌈The Fr module shall provide an XML file that contains the data, which is required
for the SW identification and configuration parameters. This file shall describe vendor
specific configuration parameters if applicable.⌋
[SWS_Fr_00480]
Upstream requirements: SRS_Fr_05058
⌈A driver MCG reads the ECU configuration parameters of the Fr and the FrIf mod-
ules. While cluster related configuration parameters are contained in the FrIf module’s
configuration, CC related configuration parameters are contained in the Fr module’s
configuration. The Fr module’s specific configuration tool shall read both ECU module
configurations to derive the configuration parameters for all FlexRay CCs mapped to
the Fr module.⌋
[SWS_Fr_00481] ⌈All frame transmission/reception related configuration parameters
are located only in the FrIf module description (within configuration containers ’FrI-
fLPdu’ and ’FrIfFrameTriggering’). The Fr must be able to handle all transmis-
sion/reception requests of all related LPdus. The LPdus within the FrIf configuration
contain both an LPduIdx which is passed to the Fr API as well as a link to a frame
triggering that holds the link of the LPdu to the FlexRay network (assignment to Slot,
channel, cycle).
The CC configuration parameters related to frame transmission and reception shall be
derived from the communication matrix the CC is mapped to within the FrIf.⌋
[SWS_Fr_00482] ⌈For optimization purposes the Fr MCG shall read the FrIf job list for
detecting the points in time certain actions on the Fr will be synchronously invoked by
the FrIf (see [6] for the FrIf configuration parameters).⌋
[SWS_Fr_00483] ⌈Based on those invocation times the Fr MCG might decide certain
resource alignment optimizations for transmission and reception (share buffers among
different LPdus).⌋
[SWS_Fr_00003] ⌈If the FrIf job list contains dedicated buffer reconfiguration entries
that allow for optimization, then the Fr module’s MCG may decide to share one buffer
for several LPdus within the static segment.⌋
[SWS_Fr_00624] ⌈If an LPdu is dynamically reconfigurable (’FrIfReconfigurable’
set to true) the MCG shall decide to assign a single exclusive hardware message buffer
to those LPdus.⌋
[SWS_Fr_00484] ⌈The Fr MCG shall have knowledge about the capabilities of the CC
and the corresponding driver, therefore this tool is called driver dependent.⌋
[SWS_Fr_00485] ⌈If an Fr MCG is unable to map all required communication opera-
tions to the available resources, then it has to report that conflict1.⌋
[SWS_Fr_00486] ⌈The number of supported FlexRay CCs is defined at configuration
time.⌋
[SWS_Fr_00487] ⌈The MCG shall ensure the consistency of the generated configura-
tion.⌋
[SWS_Fr_00027]
Upstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00345, SRS_BSW_00404
⌈The Fr module shall support the pre-compile-time and post-build-time configuration
classes.⌋
An assignment of those configuration classes to configuration parameters can be found
in Chapter 10.
Hint: The description of the software configuration itself is not part of this specification
but very implementation specific.
1This can result from either from running out of resources (e.g. buffers) or the mapping of the con-
figuration to the particular device is not supported (e.g. configuration features supported in [1], but the
device is compliant to [2]).
A detailed description of all Fr related configuration parameters is specified in
Chapter 10 of this document. Additionally the configuration parameters of the FrIf (see
chapter 10 of [6]) shall be evaluated for Fr module configuration.

7.7.5 Extended Production Errors
[SWS_Fr_00498] ⌈
Error Name:
FR_E_CTRL_TESTRESULT [_]
Short Description:
FlexRay Controller hardware error
Long Description:
This extended production error indicates hardware errors of the FlexRay
communication controller. Please note that this extended production error does
not address Flexray protocol errors detected on the network.
Fail
Every API function accessing hardware
registers of the FlexRay controller
might detect a missbehavior of the
device compared to the device
specification.
For details see requirements:
[SWS_Fr_00147], [SWS_Fr_00176],
[SWS_Fr_00181], [SWS_Fr_00520],
[SWS_Fr_00186], [SWS_Fr_00190],
[SWS_Fr_00195], [SWS_Fr_00201],
[SWS_Fr_00216], [SWS_Fr_00223],
[SWS_Fr_00613], [SWS_Fr_00232],
[SWS_Fr_00243], [SWS_Fr_00248],
[SWS_Fr_00529], [SWS_Fr_00543],
[SWS_Fr_00255], [SWS_Fr_00261],
[SWS_Fr_00552], [SWS_Fr_00560],
[SWS_Fr_00568], [SWS_Fr_00580],
[SWS_Fr_00589], [SWS_Fr_00272],
[SWS_Fr_00286], [SWS_Fr_00297],
[SWS_Fr_00308], [SWS_Fr_00319],
[SWS_Fr_00331], [SWS_Fr_00652]
Detection Criteria:
Pass
During FlexRay communication
controller initialization (function
Fr_ControllerInit()) the proper operation
of the hardware registers is
successfully verified.
For details see requirements:
[SWS_Fr_00598]
Secondary Parameters:
In case of successful device operation verification (function Fr_ControllerInit())
report PASS.
In case of an error always report FAIL.
Time Required:
If a FlexRay Controller hardware error occurs it shall be immediately reported as
error.
Monitor Frequency:
continuous
⌋()
[SWS_Fr_00600] ⌈
Error Name:
FR_E_LPDU_SLOTSTATUS [_]
Short Description:
FlexRay Protocol communication error
Long Description:
This production error indicates Flexray protocol communication errors on the
network for a particular LPdu.
▽
△
Fail
Each time FlexRay slot status with at
least one of the following FlexRay
protocol errors active:
• vSS!SyntaxError
• vSS!ContentError
• vSS!Bviolation
For details see requirements:
[SWS_Fr_00605], [SWS_Fr_00606]
Detection Criteria:
Pass
Each time FlexRay slot status with
none one of the following FlexRay
protocol errors active:
• vSS!SyntaxError
• vSS!ContentError
• vSS!Bviolation
For details see requirements:
[SWS_Fr_00627], [SWS_Fr_00629]
Secondary Parameters:
Detection of production error events is active only during ongoing FlexRay
communication.
Time Required:
The time for detecting an evident FlexRay protocol error in a particular slot
strongly depends on the period of the actual FlexRay slot and thus on the FlexRay
protocol configuration parameters.
Monitor Frequency:
continuous
⌋()

[SWS_Fr_00092] Definition of API function Fr_TransmitTxLPdu
Upstream requirements: SRS_Fr_05003, SRS_Fr_05024
⌈
Service Name
Fr_TransmitTxLPdu
Syntax
Std_ReturnType Fr_TransmitTxLPdu (
uint8 Fr_CtrlIdx,
uint16 Fr_LPduIdx,
const uint8* Fr_LSduPtr,
uint8 Fr_LSduLength,
Fr_SlotAssignmentType* Fr_SlotAssignmentPtr
)
Service ID [hex]
0x0b
Sync/Async
Asynchronous
Reentrancy
Non Reentrant for the same device
Fr_CtrlIdx
Index of FlexRay CC within the context of the FlexRay Driver.
Fr_LPduIdx
This index is used to uniquely identify a FlexRay frame.
Fr_LSduPtr
This reference points to a buffer where the assembled LSdu to be
transmitted within this LPdu is stored at.
Parameters (in)
Fr_LSduLength
Determines the length of the data (in Bytes) to be transmitted.

None

E_NOT_OK: API call aborted due to errors.

CC precondition for the function Fr_TransmitTxLPdu(): None.
[SWS_Fr_00224] ⌈The function Fr_TransmitTxLPdu() shall perform the following
tasks on FlexRay CC Fr_CtrIdx:
1. Figure out the physical resource (e.g., a buffer) mapped to the transmission of
the FlexRay frame identified by Fr_LPduIdx.
2. If FrExtendedLPduReporting is enabled and Fr_SlotAssignment is not
a NULL pointer, copy expected cycle and slot ID of the transmitted frame to
Fr_SlotAssignment.
3. If the transmit Lpdu supports dynamic payload length (configuration parame-
ter FrIfAllowDynamicLSduLength is set to true), then the transmission
resource shall be reconfigured to match the payload length Fr_LsduLength
passed to the API. Note that the dynamic payload length is only applicable to
frames within the dynamic FlexRay segment.
4. Copy Fr_LsduLength bytes from address Fr_LsduPtr into the FlexRay CC’s
transmission resource and then activate it for transmission.
5. Return E_OK.
⌋

[SWS_Fr_00588] ⌈The function Fr_GetWakeupRxStatus() shall perform the follow-
ing tasks on FlexRay CC Fr_CtrIdx:
1. Read the wakeup pattern received indicators for channel A and channel B
and write it to the output parameter Fr_WakeupRxStatusPtr. The value of
*Fr_WakeupRxStatusPtr is bitcoded with the following meaning (Bit 0 = LSB,
Bit 7 = MSB):
Bit 0 Wakeup pattern received on channel A (1), otherwise (0)
Bit 1 Wakeup pattern received on channel B (1), otherwise (0)
Bit 2 Not used (always 0)
Bit 3 Not used (always 0)
Bit 4 Not used (always 0)
Bit 5 Not used (always 0)
Bit 6 Not used (always 0)
Bit 7 Not used (always 0)
2. Reset the wakeup received indication status information within the FlexRay con-
troller.
3. Return E_OK.
⌋

procedure on the configured FlexRay channel.
2. Return E_OK.

The function Fr_SendWUP() changes the CC Fr_CtrlIdx POCState to
POC:wakeup, which is a transitional state. After wakeup procedure completion, the
CC will reach POC:ready again.
Note: Sending a wakeup pattern does not necessarily cause all cluster nodes to be
awoken afterwards. The function Fr_SendWUP() just invokes the wakeup symbol trans-
mission procedure on a certain FlexRay CC.

Zweck: Beleg aus SWS_FlexRayDriver (8.4 Function definitions).

            
8.4 Function definitions
During specification of the API functions the following guidelines were applied:
• The API functions of the Fr module shall have the return type Std_ReturnType
or void (no return code).
• If an API function of the Fr module has the return type Std_ReturnType, and if
the function performs its service successfully, then it shall return E_OK otherwise
E_NOT_OK.
• If the Fr module’s environment is passing input parameters by a reference, then
the Fr SWS shall use the const qualifier (const type *) to guarantee that it
doesn’t change the input parameter.
• For output parameters, a memory address to store the parameter is passed as
an argument.
• If API functions of the Fr module successfully finish (return E_OK), then all output
parameters shall be written with with valid values.
• If API functions of the Fr module erroneously finish (return E_NOT_OK), then no
output parameter shall be written. Output parameters shall keep their original
values in this case.

Figure 7.3: Flexray Transceiver Indexing Scheme of the FlexRay Interface In order to abstract for upper layer BSW modules the various FlexRay T ransceiver modules, which the FrIf module accesses via the FlexRay T ransceiver Driver modules, the FrIf module takes advantage of the fact that each FlexRay T ransceiver module is unambiguously assigned to a specific Channel on a specific FlexRay CC. Therefore, the FrIf module abstracts the various FlexRay T ransceivers by a combination of the two indices FrIf_CtrlIdx (Controller Index) and FrIf_ChnlIdx (Channel Index) and maps this to a tuple of FlexRay T ransceiver Driver API Service function pointer and FlexRay T ransceiver index FrT rcv_T rcvIdx. (T ransceiver Index) The function descriptions in Chapter 8 specify the required mapping of upper layer BSW module’s parameters to corresponding lower layer BSW module’s API services in detail." [SWS_FrIf_05107] Upstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00162 ⌈Besides hardware and software resources, the FrIf module also numbers the logical structure elements presented by FlexRay with an abstract, unique, zero-based consec- utive index. The static configuration data of the FrIf module contains a data structure that specifies which FlexRay CC modules and which FlexRay T ransceiver modules are connected to which Clusters, or in other words, that maps each value of FrIf_ClstIdx to (one, or in general) a set of values for FrIf_CtrlIdx and tuples of (FrIfCtrlIIdx, FrIf_ChnlIdx). ⌋

Zweck: Beleg aus SWS_OS (12.6 Migration from OIL to XML).

            
12.6 Migration from OIL to XML
This version of the AUTOSAR OS specification does not directly support the config-
uration via OIL. The support for OIL was dropped in favour of XML because XML is
the standard configuration language in AUTOSAR and is essential if configuration data
has to be imported / exported from / to other AUTOSAR modules or between different
tools during development.
Since OIL and XML are both ASCII formats a tool vendor may offer a possibility to
import (old) OIL files and to store them as (AUTOSAR OS) XML files. Currently all
known vendors support at least the import of existing OIL configurations.
Note that for showing conformance to the OSEK OS specification, each OSEK OS ven-
dor must support OIL. This means that practically each AUTOSAR OS vendor will offer
some sort of import of OIL configurations - at least to show the OSEK OS conformance.

Zweck: Beleg aus SWS_OS (12.8 Integration hints for peripheral protection).

            
12.8 Integration hints for peripheral protection
Peripheral protection requires configuration on the core level usually conditioned by a
supervisor access. For this reason the task of the peripheral protection is assigned to
the OS module.
Peripheral protection may be implemented in two ways
- using MPU
- using dedicated peripheral protection units of the target MCU.
When using the memory protection unit, it is reasonable if two or more protected region
descriptors are available for peripheral protection mechanism. The region descriptors
shall be programmed to allow access to those peripherals the current OS-Application
shall work with. The defined regions shall cover all memory mapped configuration
registers for the periphiherals to be protected. The advantage of using the MPU is that
the configuration is the same as for memory protection. One of the disadvantages of
this method is that it could be impossilbe to cover all peripheral control registers with
available MPU region descriptors. The number of such descriptors is typically low.
Beware that using this method may have implication to the linker file of the project
software configuration.
Second method is using a dedicated register protection schema. This method shall
allow to precisely select peripherals for every OS Application. However the number of
peripherals may make the register protection implementation rather bulky. Therefore it
is advisable to reduce the number of protected peripherals to a reasonable value.
For both methods the configuration shall be placed into custom OS Application prop-
erties. The configuration shall be active when a Task (or ISR) of a particular OS
Application is running.

Zweck: Beleg aus SWS_OS (12.9 Termination of OS-Applications).

            
12.9 Termination of OS-Applications
Inconsistencies may occur when an OsApplication is terminated and restarted, de-
pending on its state at the termination.
• A notification from an asynchronous job started before the termination of OsAp-
plication can occur after the restart of OsApplication.
• An asynchronous memory read or write started before the termination of OsAp-
plication can occur after restart, and cause data inconsistency.
• A requested mode or state to another OsApplication (e.g. from a SW-C to
A BSW) can lead to unsynchronized state machines after an OsApplication
restart.
Therefore some measures shall be taken to avoid these inconsistencies and guaranty
a correct behavior.
Integration code shall stop all signals and signalgroups during its OsApplication
restart. This ensures that no late asynchronous notification will occur after the OsAp-
plication restart. These signals and signalgroups can be then safely restarted if
needed.
A SW-C shall cancel jobs on all its memory blocks with a call to NvM_CancelJobs
during the restart of its OsApplication. As the job might have already been started,
the call to NvM_CancelJobs can return an error; in that case, the OsApplication
shall wait until end of the job to continue. After all jobs are ensured to be cancelled, then
all memory blocks shall be reset to their initial value, in order to avoid inconsistency of
data which might have been written before the cancellation.
Any SW-C having responsible for requesting mode or state to BSW mode managers
shall always request a default mode upon a restart of its OsApplication. Thus the
BSW mode manager would not be stuck into a mode previously requested by the
OsApplication before its termination. To support this task, note that RTE offers
mechanisms to handle partition stop and restart wrt. mode machines. For mode man-
agers an "error mode" to be set by RTE can be identified. For mode user partition
the behaviour can also be selected. Furthermore an interaction to BswM to trigger an
action list in case of partition restart can be initiated. Refer to RTE specification for
details.
As a global hint, in any non-trusted OsApplication, which could be terminated, there
shall always be a restart Task which does the following actions:
• Cancel all jobs which can result in an asynchronous notification or shared mem-
ory, I/O access.
• Reset all shared memory with a default value.
• Reset any mode or state residing in another OsApplication and controlled by
this given OsApplication to a default value.
Please note that some of these actions need to be performed even if an OS-Application
is merely terminated and not restarted. For example, it may still be necessary to stop
all signals and signal groups used by the OsApplication. Otherwise, it may happen
that a bus never goes to sleep.
Consequently, in such a case it is necessary to activate the restart Task to perform
the necessary cleanup even if the OS-Application is only terminated and not restarted.
Calling TerminateApplication(,OS_OSAPPLICATION_NO_RESTART)
in the restart Task will finally set the OS-Application to APPLICATION_TERMINATED.

Zweck: Beleg aus SWS_FlexRayISOTransportLayer (14 The available data length evaluation depends on different scenarios the FrTp is used in.).

            
14  The available data length evaluation depends on different scenarios the FrTp is used in.
- In case of a normal ECU which transfers data with unknown message lengths it is necessary to
evaluate the length of the currently stored FrTp-N-SDU.
- In case an ECU transmits data with known message length the Tx data length is given by the
parameter of the FrTp_Transmit service primitive. An additional evaluation by calling
PduR_FrTpCopyTxData(..) is possible to have equal evaluation sequences for known and
unknown message length transfers but could be skipped by runtime optimisation (implementation
dependency).
- In case of a Gateway which routes N-SDUs of different bus systems it is necessary to get the
currently available (received) data length in the gateway buffer.

Zweck: Beleg aus SWS_FlexRayISOTransportLayer (15 FrTp transmits always the real amount of data stored in the corresponding buffer. FrTp is not).

            
15 FrTp transmits always the real amount of data stored in the corresponding buffer. FrTp is not

Step 11 - 12
If the N-PDU was successfully transmitted by the FrIf module, the FrIf module shall
call the service primitive FrTp_TxConfirmation with result E_OK. Within this
service primitive the FrTp module shall reset the state of the corresponding
FrTpTxPdu.

⌈The service primitive FrTp_TxConfirmation shall be

[SWS_FrTp_01054]
⌈The service primitive FrTp_TxConfirmation shall
reset the state of the corresponding FrTpTxPdu (N-PDU) to “idle”. ⌋()
Step 13 - 16
Depending on ISO-10681-2 protocol handling in some cases a response N-PDU
(Flow Control) from the receiver is expected by the sender. Hence the sender has to
wait until the response N-PDU (Flow Control) is received and continue processing
after reception.
[SWS_FrTp_01055]
⌈The FrTp module shall implement a timing and timeout
behaviour as defined in chapter 7.5.8⌋()
Step 17 - 21
If all N-SDU data are transmitted the FrTp module shall free all allocated resources
and reset all flags which signals an ongoing data transfer for this connection.
If the data transmission is pending, the FrTp module shall continue the data transfer
at step 6.

The FlexRay NM MainFunction will hold the "automated" functionality of the FlexRay

NM-Messages and the periodic processing of the FlexRay NM state machine (at the
boundary between two NM-Repetition Cycles).

figured within the FlexRay Interface.

2.4.4 API Function Parameters
[TR_BSWMG_00020] API Function Parameters ⌈The function parameters shall have
mandatory entries for “Name”, “Type”, “Direction” and “Notes”.⌋()
[TR_BSWMG_00032] API Function Parameter types ⌈The parameter “Type” shall be
one of the existing types defined in the BSW model.⌋()
[TR_BSWMG_00033] C-Style Pointers as API Function Parameters ⌈Parameters
may be modeled as C-Style pointers by appending * to the parameter type, e.g.
PduInfoType*⌋()
[TR_BSWMG_00027] Mandatory pointers for API Function Output Parameters
⌈Parameters must be modeled as pointers if their “Direction” attribute is set to out or
inout.⌋()
[TR_BSWMG_00035] Mandatory constant types for pointers of API Function In-
put Parameters ⌈Pointer-type parameters of direction type “in", i.e. parameters that
represent read-only structures or arrays, may prepend the parameter type with the
const keyword. This enforces that the data pointed to by the parameter is read-only
and will not be altered by the function. Example: const FrIf_ConfigType*⌋()
[TR_BSWMG_00021] API Function Parameter Direction ⌈The parameter’s direction
type attribute shall be set to one of the values in, out, inout, return.⌋()
[TR_BSWMG_00022] API Function Parameter Description ⌈Each parameter shall
provide a short description about its purpose.⌋()
Note: EA provides a textfield called ‘Notes’ to take the parameters description.
[TR_BSWMG_00023] API Function Return Parameter ⌈If the function’s return type
is not equal to void, the return value shall be modeled like an operation parameter
with the following exceptions: It shall be the first parameter in the list. Additionally, it
shall be the only parameter to have its “Direction” set to “return”. The notes field shall
concisely describe the possible return values.⌋()
Modeling Guidelines of Basic Software EA UML
Model
Figure 2.5: Parameter example of a API function
[TR_BSWMG_00922] API Function Return Value Links ⌈All possible return values
for an API function’s return parameter that are described in the notes field of the pa-
rameter shall be linked to the definition of the value.
In particular, if the function’s return type is a simple type (see [TR_BSWMG_00066])
the link shall be put as
[ARDataTypeElement{}{}].
If it is an enumeration (see [TR_BSWMG_00072]) the link shall be put as
[AREnumLiteral{}{}].
Note
that

shall
be
set
to
the
anchor
name
(see
[TR_BSWMG_00031]) of the datatype if one is defined.⌋()
Example: The correct way to link the return values in the example of Figure 2.5 is to
put this description into the notes field of the return parameter:
[ARDataTypeElement{E_OK}{Std_ReturnType}]: Cancellation of request timeout was successful

[ARDataTypeElement{E_NOT_OK}{Std_ReturnType}]: Cancellation of request timeout was not
successful
Note: If the return type has an extension (as defined in 2.4.8.3) then always the type
in the model defining the current value has to be linked.
Example: If an API function in the Csm module returns the Std_ReturnType then e.g.
values E_OK and CRYPTO_E_BUSY may be returned as the latter value is defined
in Csm_ReturnType, which is an extension to Std_ReturnType. In that case the links
have to be set like this:
[ARDataTypeElement{E_OK}{Std_ReturnType}]: ...

[ARDataTypeElement{CRYPTO_E_BUSY}{Csm_ReturnType}]: ...
Modeling Guidelines of Basic Software EA UML
Model
[TR_BSWMG_00129] Optional Parameters of API Functions ⌈The existence of a
parameter may depend on the module configuration. In this case, the parameter shall
have the stereotype ≪optional≫.⌋()
[TR_BSWMG_00130] Multiplicity of API Function Parameters ⌈A parameter with a
given type may occur several times, where the multiplicity is specified by configuration.
In this case, the parameter shall have the stereotype ≪multiple≫.⌋()
Hint: Don’t use the multiplicity button in the parameter edit mask to configure the mul-
tiplicity.
[TR_BSWMG_00131] Mutual Exclusive Variants of API Function Parameters ⌈A
parameter may appear in different variants within the same position of the function
signature, where one specific variant will be selected by configuration. In this case, the
parameter shall be modeled several times in all its possible variants and each variant
of the parameter shall have the stereotype ≪mutualexcl≫.⌋()
Example: The parameter “buffer” of the Xfrm function “_” can
be configured either as “inout” or “out”. It therefore shall be modeled two times, one
time with Direction “inout” and the second time with Direction “out”. Since Enterprise
Architect requires parameter names to be unique, the first parameter variant may be
named “buffer{inout}” and the second one “buffer{out}”.
Hint: All variants of a mutual exclusive parameter shall have the same name; the name
without the curly brackets (including the text) have to be the same.
Figure 2.6: Mutual Exclusive Parameter example of a API function
Modeling Guidelines of Basic Software EA UML
Model

5.2 FlexRay Interface
The following services of the FlexRay Interface are called by the FlexRay AUTOSAR
Transport Layer module:
 FrIf_Transmit
By this API service, the sending of a frame (N-PDU) is triggered. Depending
on configuration on the FlexRay Interface, the N-PDU is sent immediately or
after the call of FrArTp_TriggerTransmit.
The following services of the FlexRay AUTOSAR Transport Layer module are called
by the FlexRay Interface:
 FrArTp_RxIndication
By this API service, the FlexRay Interface indicates the reception of an FrArTp
frame (N-PDU, please do not mistake this with a FlexRay frame) to the
FrArTp. The FrArTp then processes this frame.
 FrArTp_TxConfirmation
By this API service, the FlexRay Interface confirms the (un)successful sending
of the frame containing the N-PDU over the FlexRay network.
 FrArTp_TriggerTransmit
By this API service, the FlexRay Interface makes the FrArTp to copy the N-
PDU into the buffer provided by the FlexRay Interface. The FlexRay interface
then can start sending the FlexRay frame containing the N-PDU.

5.3 FlexRay Interface
The following services primitives of the FlexRay Interface (FrIf) module are called by
the FrTp:
 FrIf_Transmit
By this API service primitive, the transfer of an Fr N-PDU is initiated.
The following services primitives of the FrTp module are called by the FlexRay
Interface module:
 FrTp_RxIndication
By this API service primitive, the FlexRay Interface module indicates the
reception of an FrTp frame (Fr N-PDU, not to be confused with a FlexRay
frame) to the FrTp. The FrTp then processes this frame.
 FrTp_TxConfirmation
By this API service primitive, the FlexRay Interface module confirms the
sending of the frame containing the Fr N-PDU with result (E_OK if the
transmission was successful, E_NOT_OK if the transmission failed) over the
FlexRay network.
 FrTp_TriggerTransmit
By this API service primitive, the FlexRay Interface get access to the Fr N-
PDU data.1

Zweck: Beleg aus SWS_PDURouter (5 Dependencies to other modules).

            
5 Dependencies to other modules
The PDU Router module depends on the APIs and capabilities of the used communi-
cation hardware abstraction layer modules and the used communication service layer
modules. Basically the API functions required by the PDU Router module are:
Communication Interface modules:
• _Transmit (e.g. CanIf_Transmit, FrIf_Transmit, LinIf_Trans-
mit)
• _CancelTransmit (e.g. FrIf_CancelTransmit)
Transport Protocol Modules:
• _Transmit (e.g.
CanTp_Transmit,
FrTp_Transmit,
LinTp_
Transmit)
• _CancelTransmit (e.g.
CanTp_CancelTransmit, FrTp_Cancel
Transmit)
• _CancelReceive (e.g. CanTp_CancelReceive, FrTp_CancelRe-
ceive)
Upper layer modules which use Transport Protocol modules:
• _StartOfReception (e.g. Dcm_StartOfReception)
• _CopyRxData (e.g. Dcm_CopyRxData)
• _CopyTxData (e.g. Dcm_CopyTxData)
• _TpRxIndication (e.g. Dcm_TpRxIndication)
• _TpTxConfirmation (e.g. Dcm_TpTxConfirmation)
Upper layer modules which process I-PDUs originating from Communication Interface
modules:
• _RxIndication (e.g. Com_RxIndication),
• _TxConfirmation (e.g. Com_TxConfirmation),
• _TriggerTransmit (e.g. Com_TriggerTransmit)

7.3.1 FlexRay Interface Main Function
The FlexRay Interface Main Function needs to be called cyclically from a task body pro-
vided by the BSW Scheduler with a calling period (FRIF_MAINFUNCTION_PERIOD)
depending on the FlexRay Cycle length and configurable at system configuration time.
Since the Cycle length of each Cluster is independent, the desired calling period of
the FlexRay Interface Main Function might differ from Cluster to Cluster, except for
"Transmission with Immediate Buffer Access".
[SWS_FrIf_05119]
Upstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00432
⌈The FrIf module shall provide one dedicated FlexRay Interface Main Function for each
FlexRay Cluster that is controlled by that FrIf module.⌋
[SWS_FrIf_05283]
Upstream requirements: SRS_BSW_00373
⌈The API names of the FlexRay Interface Main Functions shall obey the following pat-
tern:
FrIf_MainFunction_
where
FrIfCluster.ShortName
is
the
Short Name of the corresponding FrIfCluster.⌋
[SWS_FrIf_15120] ⌈The Main Function monitors and controls the continuous execu-
tion of the FlexRay Job List Execution Function including the (re)synchronization if the
current FlexRay Interface State Machine is FRIF_STATE_ONLINE.⌋
[SWS_FrIf_01124] ⌈If Bus Mirroring is enabled globally (see FrIfBusMirroringSupport),
then call Fr_GetChannelStatus for all controllers of each FlexRay cluster for which mir-
roring has been activated with a call to FrIf_EnableBusMirroring(), merge the states
reported for the controllers of one cluster with a binary OR, and then call Mirror_Re-
portFlexRayChannelStatus() with the cluster, Fr_ChannelAStatusPtr, and Fr_Channel
BStatusPtr to report the aggregated channel states to the Bus Mirroring module.⌋
[SWS_FrIf_25120] ⌈If one of the optional cluster-specific configuration parameters
FRIF_E_NIT_CH_A, FRIF_E_NIT_CH_B, FRIF_E_SW_CH_A, FRIF_E_SW_CH_B or
FRIF_E_ACS_CH_A, FRIF_E_ACS_CH_B exists, then call FrIf_GetChannelStatus for
each FlexRay controller of the cluster and report the status to DEM as described be-
low.⌋
[SWS_FrIf_35120] ⌈If the optional configuration parameter FRIF_E_NIT_CH_A ex-
ists, then the channel status information shall be reported to DEM as Dem_Set
EventStatus (FRIF_E_NIT_CH_A, DEM_EVENT_STATUS_PREFAILED) when any of
the error bits of a single controller (Channel A NIT status data vSS!SyntaxError, v
SS!Bviolation) is set or as Dem_SetEventStatus (FRIF_E_NIT_CH_A, DEM_EVENT_
STATUS_PREPASSED) when none of these error bits is set.⌋
[SWS_FrIf_45120] ⌈If the optional configuration parameter FRIF_E_NIT_CH_B ex-

SS!Bviolation, vSS!TxConflict) is set or as Dem_SetEventStatus (FRIF_E_SW_CH_A,
DEM_EVENT_STATUS_PREPASSED) when none of these error bits is set.⌋
[SWS_FrIf_65120] ⌈If the optional configuration parameter FRIF_E_SW_CH_B exists,

Status (FRIF_E_ACS_CH_A , DEM_EVENT_STATUS_PREFAILED) when any of the
error bits of a single controller (Channel A aggregated channel status vSS!SyntaxEr-
ror, vSS!ContentError, vSS!Bviolation, vSS!TxConflict) is set or as Dem_SetEventSta-
tus (FRIF_E_ACS_CH_A, DEM_EVENT_STATUS_PREPASSED) when none of these
error bits is set.⌋
[SWS_FrIf_85120] ⌈If the optional configuration parameter FRIF_E_ACS_CH_B ex-
ists, then the channel status information shall be reported to DEM as Dem_SetEvent
Status (FRIF_E_ACS_CH_B, DEM_EVENT_STATUS_PREFAILED) when any of the
error bits of a single controller (Channel B aggregated channel status vSS!SyntaxEr-
ror, vSS!ContentError, vSS!Bviolation, vSS!TxConflict) is set or as Dem_SetEventSta-
tus (FRIF_E_ACS_CH_B, DEM_EVENT_STATUS_PREPASSED) when none of these
error bits is set.⌋
[SWS_FrIf_95120] ⌈If a loss of the JobList’s synchronization (see JobListAsyncFlag)
or a miss of execution was detected, the following steps shall be performed:
1. Get the global time (FrIf_GetGlobalTime())
• If FrIf_GetGlobalTime() returns E_NOT_OK, stop here
• If FrIf_GetGlobalTime() returns E_OK, continue with step 2
2. add some ’time buffer’ (i.e. some timespan which takes jitter into account)
3. search the FlexRay Job List for the next job, i.e. that job with an invocation time
greater than the current global time + ’time buffer’.
4. set the JobListPointer to that job and program the absolute timer with this job’s
invocation time (now the FlexRay Job List is synchronized again)
5. clear the JobListAsyncFlag
6. Enable the absolute timer interrupt
⌋
